detail.abstract: The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping the U.S. labor market by transforming job tasks, workplace processes, and the skills needed for effective performance. This study examines AI-driven occupational transformation, evolving employer skill requirements, and the growing importance of AI, digital, analytical, and social capabilities in the U.S. workforce. Drawing on research related to automation, technological change, AI exposure, and labor-market skill demand, the study assesses the implications of AI adoption for workforce reskilling and upskilling (Acemoglu & Restrepo, 2018, 2019, 2020; Alekseeva et al., 2021; Eloundou et al., 2024). Employing a structured literature-based methodology, the study synthesizes evidence from labor-market analyses, occupational exposure assessments, job-posting research, and workforce-development literature. The analysis indicates that AI is unlikely to eliminate employment but is expected to transform task composition and increase demand for workers who possess a combination of technical, analytical, creative, interpersonal, and adaptive skills (Bankins et al., 2024; Green, 2024). The findings further suggest that effective labor force adaptation requires coordinated action among employers, educational institutions, governments, and training providers. The study concludes that the United States must establish an accessible, continuous reskilling ecosystem that integrates AI literacy, technical capabilities, human-centered skills, employer-led training, and lifelong learning opportunities to prepare workers for an increasingly AI-enabled digital economy.

title: Recruiting Talent, Recruiting Bodies: Cultural Content and the Two Margins of Criminal Entry

detail.title: Recruiting Talent, Recruiting Bodies: Cultural Content and the Two Margins of Criminal Entry

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no financial or non-financial conflicts of interest related to this research. No party with a stake in narcocorrido regulation, criminal justice policy, streaming platforms, or the Mexican or Brazilian music industries funded, reviewed, or influenced any part of this work.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. All data are from publicly available sources (INEGI mortality microdata, web search indexes). The author received no compensation from any organization for this work.

detail.abstract: Narcocorridos come in two kinds. The traditional corrido narrates the successful trafficker; the bélico subgenre glorifies the instruments of violence. A companion paper argues that criminal-glorifying music resolves an organization's adverse-selection problem by pricing criminal prestige on success. This paper asks which content does what. The answer is a theorem about timing: a reward collected on success is worth more to those likely to succeed, so it changes who enters; a reward collected on participation is worth the same to everyone, so it changes how many enter. The data deliver the predicted pattern across 148 Mexican municipalities over 2012-2024. Traditional salience predicts the educational composition of homicide victims and the bélico does not; bélico salience is the stronger predictor of the number of victims, as the model requires. The composition result survives municipality fixed effects and is directional in time; the scale result is cross-sectional only and moves both ways, with violence and violent content feeding each other. The two contents are complements in production, jointly supplied by organizations recruiting for two roles. The performance bans spreading across Mexico target the content that recruits bodies and miss the content that recruits talent.

title: Price-State Resolvability and Algorithmic Collusion in Kyle Markets

detail.title: Price-State Resolvability and Algorithmic Collusion in Kyle Markets

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests. The paper studies the environment of Dou, Goldstein, and Ji (2025); the author has no affiliation with those authors or with any organization with an interest in the findings, and no relationship with any trading firm, exchange, or regulator whose activities are discussed. No party other than the author had any role in the design, execution, analysis, or reporting of the study, or any right of review over the manuscript prior to submission.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. The work was conducted using the author's own institutional resources at the Beedie School of Business, Simon Fraser University.

detail.abstract: Collusion under imperfect public monitoring requires that deviations affect the signals observed by coordinating agents. For reinforcement-learning traders, this condition depends not only on the underlying market signal but also on how that signal is represented in the learner's state space. We define price-state resolvability as the probability that a unilateral deviation changes the discretized price state observed by another learner. The Kyle-style market of Dou, Goldstein, and Ji (2025) provides a natural laboratory because traders condition on a discretized public price, making monitoring jointly determined by price informativeness and state representation. Varying the construction and resolution of the price partition reveals a tradeoff between detection and learning. When deviations are difficult to detect, greater resolvability strengthens coordination, and partitions preserving similar amounts of deviation information produce similar outcomes. Once deviations are readily observable, however, finer partitions weaken coordination by spreading the experience needed to learn punishment across more post-deviation states. A fixed-cardinality experiment shows that the relevant margin is the price movement induced by a deviation relative to bin width: coordination is strongest near the point at which deviations become reliably observable. The learned strategies deter the canonical one-period deviation but fail a full dynamic best-response test, with gains from reoptimization increasing with learned coordination. Finally, we separate the effect of market noise on price informativeness from its effect on discrete-state resolvability. Preserving the learner's ability to observe deviations does not restore punishment-supported coordination, implying that the decline is driven by worsening price informativeness rather than discretization. At higher noise, comparable observability requires partitions fine enough to impede the learning of punishment. Coordination nevertheless re-emerges only after the punishment response has disappeared, consistent with Dou, Goldstein, and Ji's (2025) interpretation of the high-noise region as over-pruning rather than price-trigger punishment.

detail.abstract: We study robust incentive design for independently acting agents when the principal lacks knowledge of both their feasible actions and the resulting output distributions. The principal observes one reference action per agent and its coarse information, then minimizes worstcase regret relative to the contract she would choose under full knowledge of the technology. Every continuous deterministic contract is weakly regret-dominated by its endpoint linearization in gross-utility space. An optimal deterministic contract can therefore be chosen to align agents' rankings without imposing alignment, while monetary compensation may remain nonlinear. We derive an exact finite-dimensional r egret c haracterization a nd identify the trade-off between unnecessary compensation and missed productive opportunities. For symmetric two-agent teams, an optimum can be chosen either symmetric or fully concentrated. In a separate characterized multi-agent region, minimax regret motivates every member, whereas max-min appoints one lead agent.

title: Does Testing Environment Matter? Evidence From a Quasi-Experiment in Introductory Accounting
affiliations: University of South Dakota - School of Business and University of South Dakota

detail.title: Does Testing Environment Matter? Evidence From a Quasi-Experiment in Introductory Accounting

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No Personal or Financial Relationships to Declare.
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: This study examines whether changes in supervisory environment are associated with differential changes in student examination performance. Using two concurrently taught sections of introductory accounting, a simple quasi-experimental design compares a treatment group that transitions from remote monitored testing to direct in-person supervision with a control group that remains under remote monitored testing. Both groups complete identical examinations under the same note policy, with the primary difference being the mode of supervision. Results reveal significant differences in performance changes across groups, including an estimated difference-in-differences effect of 10.8 percent. These findings suggest that supervisory environment may influence observed examination performance and highlight the importance of considering testing conditions when designing assessments and comparing student learning outcomes across instructional modalities.

title: Quantifying Sustainability for Structured Credit Products: An NLP-Driven ESG Scoring Approach
affiliations: University College London and University College London

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Budha Bhattacharya is employed by Lombard Odier Investment Management and is affiliated with University College London. Francesca Medda is affiliated with University College London. The authors declare no other financial or personal relationships that could have influenced the research presented in this paper.

detail.abstract: This paper develops an Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) scoring methodology for structured credit products, with a particular focus on Commercial Mortgage-Backed Securities (CMBS). Conventional ESG frameworks are largely issuer-centric, whereas securitisations distribute economically relevant risks across originators, underwriters, servicers, trustees, borrowers and collateral. The proposed framework combines document-level natural language processing (NLP) for entity and role extraction with structured ESG information, role-based hierarchical weighting, and a news/controversy component. Zero-shot classification, transformer models (BERT/RoBERTa) and large language models are positioned as complementary tools for converting unstructured transaction documentation into an auditable entity-role representation. The methodology further incorporates entity resolution, parent mapping, confidence-aware data governance and temporal smoothing. A Freddie Mac Green Bond CMBS example illustrates the mechanics of the workflow and score decomposition. Numerical ESG and sentiment values in the case study are explicitly hypothetical placeholders; the application is a methodological demonstration rather than statistical validation. The contribution is therefore an instrument-aware, explainable architecture for sustainability assessment in structured credit, together with a research agenda for empirical calibration and cross-asset validation.

title: The Praxeological Problem of "Store of Value": Austrian Monetary Theory, Tax Friction, and the Financialized Enclosure of Bitcoin

detail.title: The Praxeological Problem of "Store of Value": Austrian Monetary Theory, Tax Friction, and the Financialized Enclosure of Bitcoin

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant or financial support from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: This paper argues, from within the Austrian praxeological tradition, that the popular "store of value first" account of Bitcoin's monetization does not survive that tradition's own premises. Its central, theoretical claim is that money's store-of-value function cannot be treated as severable from an asset's contemporaneous salability in exchange, and that the stage-theory popularized by Saifedean Ammous conflates a genuine Mengerian phenomenon—hoarding driven by anticipation of future exchange—with something Menger never describes: value storage severed from any exchange prospect at all. Rather than bracket the regression-theorem dispute between William Luther and George Pickering, this paper takes a position: even granting Pickering's more permissive reading, under which Bitcoin's initial exchange value required only subjective anticipation of a future medium-of-exchange role, that anticipation has to be renewed continuously by the market to sustain monetary status; it cannot be secured once at Bitcoin's origin and coast indefinitely. Whether contemporary demand renews it is an empirical question, and the paper's finding—drawn from transaction patterns, El Salvador's abandoned legal-tender experiment, Germany's decade of tax-friction-free holding, and the concentration of Bitcoin exchange-traded-fund custody—is that it largely does not: the evidence is substantially more consistent with speculative and institutional-allocation demand than with monetary reservation demand. A further claim concerns mechanism. U.S. capital-gains taxation of every Bitcoin disposition, and the SEC's Staff Accounting Bulletin No. 121, which for nearly three years made large-scale institutional Bitcoin custody prohibitively capital-intensive for regulated banks, together help explain why Bitcoin's use has drifted toward one-way financialized exposure rather than the peer-to-peer medium of exchange its founding literature described.

detail.abstract: LLMs used for trading emit reasoning traces opaque to humans but parsable by other LLMs. How does this hidden channel reshape tacit collusion in financial markets? I embed pre-trade leakage in a market with informed traders and a competitive market maker. Leakage sharpens posteriors about fundamental value and renders the rival's intended order predictable. Both channels (information and enforcement) relax the repeated-game incentive constraint and expand the sustainable-collusion set. Q-learning and production-LLM experiments verify the mechanism; mitigation is explored. The analysis suggests LLM deployment can expand the sustainablecollusion frontier; welfare cost falls hardest where price-based monitoring is weakest.

title: The Operational, Financial, and Business Benefits of Permissionless Blockchains over Permissioned Networks for Users and Regulators
affiliations: Columbia University - Columbia Business School

detail.title: The Operational, Financial, and Business Benefits of Permissionless Blockchains over Permissioned Networks for Users and Regulators

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The research contained in this paper and the ideas expressed by it are exclusive to the author.
declarations.funderStatement: This paper was prepared with financial support from Coinbase. The author benefited from conversations about the topic with the sponsoring organization, but the opinions, analysis, and conclusions are solely his—they were not vetted by anyone. The sponsor did not propose the subject to the author, nor did it have any rights of editorial approval on the final content. Any errors are the author’s responsibility.

detail.abstract:
Growing adoption of cryptocurrencies, stablecoins, and other tokenized assets raises the important question of which type of platform such assets should rely on: permissionless platforms such as Bitcoin and Ethereum where participation in consensus is open to all, or enterprise networks where participation is permissioned and controlled by a gatekeeper. 

This paper describes the technical and practical differences between the two types of networks. It explains why permissionless systems offer desirable properties such as resilience, minimized counterparty risk, and guaranteed settlement, and lays out the mechanical process by which the reintroduction of a gatekeeper forfeits those benefits. It argues that permissioned systems are not blockchains and that the assets tracked by them should not be considered tokens. 

The paper further compares each design to how legacy payment and capital market systems operate. It argues that permissionless systems are a safer and more innovative upgrade, requiring minimal regulation for responsible adoption. It then demonstrates how permissioned systems are closer to existing systems in operational and financial risk, requiring complex new regulations to maintain stability, protect users, and avoid regulatory arbitrage. 

Lastly, the paper contemplates the business implications of the two approaches and shows how enterprise networks are likely to mirror the monopoly power and "too big to fail" dynamics that plague legacy systems, discriminating against smaller entities and startups in favor of large incumbents. It argues for the adoption of permissionless systems as an opportunity to break this paradigm.

title: Which Tax Incentives Survive Pillar Two? A Comparative Simulation of QDMTT Exposure Across Six Incentive Archetypes

detail.title: Which Tax Incentives Survive Pillar Two? A Comparative Simulation of QDMTT Exposure Across Six Incentive Archetypes

declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study does not involve human participants, patient data, or personal data. It is a purely theoretical tax simulation using publicly available OECD Model Rules and illustrative numerical examples only. No ethics approval required.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding. This research is self-funded by the author as independent research. No grant or institutional funding was received.

detail.abstract: The OECD/G20 Pillar Two framework does not treat all tax incentives equally: whether an incentive survives a 15% global minimum tax depends less on its generosity than on its legal architecture. This paper extends prior jurisdiction-specific simulation work (Lanke, 2026) to build a comparative taxonomy of six incentive archetypes-income-based exemptions, preferential rate elections, qualified refundable tax credits (QRTCs), non-qualified tax credits, accelerated depreciation, and IP/patent box regimes-and simulates each archetype's post-QDMTT effective tax rate under a common GloBE Income base. The results show a stark bifurcation: income-based exemptions and non-qualified credits are compressed toward the 15% floor, while QRTCs, by design, are treated as GloBE Income rather than as reductions of Covered Taxes and therefore generally preserve more incentive value. Accelerated depreciation sits in between, generating a timing rather than a permanent difference. The paper's practical contribution is a simple decision framework host-country policymakers can use to redesign investment incentives for continued effectiveness post-Pillar Two, and its academic contribution is a unified simulation structure that the author's ongoing doctoral research extends into firm-level empirical testing of investment responses to this archetype-dependent compression pattern.

detail.abstract: According to Blecker (2027), while tariffs per se are not always and everywhere unwarranted (Blecker, 2026), the Trump tariffs will fail on their own terms. Making this argument necessitates suspending disbelief, so as to interpret the Trump tariffs as economic policy-something that various commentators, who regard the tariffs as no more than political theatre, refuse to indulge. The argument here is that distinguishing between political chicanery and economics in this fashion involves a false dichotomy. Acknowledging the potential relationship between the two permits analysis that points towards an unpleasant political economy rationale for the Trump tariffs.

All participants provided informed consent online before taking part. The experiment was preregistered on AsPredicted (#293,246).

detail.abstract: Models of motivated cognition assume that agents selectively direct their attention to improve their mood, confidence, or anticipatory utility, and yet the modern attention economy appears dominated by negativity. We study this tension in a controlled experiment. Participants take a selfie and then work on a real-effort task while a feed of comments about their appearance, resembling those on social media, are posted alongside their task. Ex ante, participants overwhelmingly prefer this feed to be populated primarily by positive, complimentary comments. In the moment, however, this preference reverses: when exposed to a feed composed of both positive and negative comments, they engage significantly more with the negative content. Consistent with participants knowing their consumption of negative comments is compulsive, a third of participants are willing to pay a strictly positive price for a positive rather than a negative feed, and they ex post regret reading negative comments more than positive comments. This asymmetry between ex ante and in-the-moment attention preferences is larger among women, who report caring more about their appearance, consistent with concerns that social media usage may be particularly harmful for young women.

title: Do Tax Judges Favor the Tax Authority?
affiliations: University of Oregon - School of Law

detail.title: Do Tax Judges Favor the Tax Authority?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: Judges and judicial systems have become more specialized in response to increasing legal complexity. While the theoretical literature has discussed judicial specialization extensively, deliberating its pros and cons and its implications-arguably an appealing background for empirical investigation-few empirical studies have attempted to quantify the relationship between judicial specialization and case outcomes. This Article fills that lacuna. It analyzes a hand-coded dataset of tax cases in which rulings were made by both specialized tax judges and generalist judges in Israeli District Courts. Its main finding is that specialized tax judges are more inclined than generalist judges toward the Tax Authority. It also finds that women judges and judges who worked in the private sector before their nomination are more inclined toward the Tax Authority than men judges and judges who were part of the public sector before taking the bench.

detail.abstract: Korea is undergoing rapid population aging, with 32.8% of older adults living alone, raising urgent needs for safety and emotional support. However, public care resources, such as social workers, remain limited. To address this gap, the Korean government launched an artificial intelligence-based Companion Call Service (AI Call Service) that provides AI-initiated check-in calls to older adults and routes flagged cases to human follow-up. This study examined older adults' experiences with the AI Call Service to explore how AI-assisted care complements human care. We used a mixed-methods design combining a survey of 500 older adults (61.8% female; 79.2% living alone; approximately 11% of all service users) with focus group interviews involving service users and frontline staff to examine experiences of AI-assisted care. The 2024 survey revealed that 90% of respondents expressed overall satisfaction, citing reassurance, relief from boredom, and a sense of companionship from AI-initiated conversations. 5.6% of participants received a human follow-up after the AI flagged a risk factor, primarily due to missed multiple calls. Across both focus groups, frontline staff and users described the AI Call Service as a human-centered, complementary form of care that alleviates loneliness through relational interactions while facilitating risk monitoring.

title: Poverty and Biased Evaluations of Uncertainty: Theory and Experimental Evidence

detail.abstract: This paper shows that biased evaluations of uncertainty generate a poverty trap. I develop a theoretical framework to study how probability weighting, a welldocumented bias in decision making under uncertainty, shapes investment decisions among the poor. The model predicts that probability weighting can lead individuals to forgo investments that are profitable in expectation, and that poverty amplifies this tendency. Probability weighting therefore creates a self-reinforcing mechanism: low wealth makes distorted probability evaluations more consequential for investment decisions, and the resulting underinvestment perpetuates low wealth. I provide empirical evidence for this mechanism using two experiments conducted on representative samples of American households and a randomized controlled trial in Bangladesh.

detail.abstract:
This technical supplement evaluates the empirical basis, reproducibility, sensitivity, external-source validation, and cross-city transferability of the Structural Intensity (SI) threshold SI ≥ 0.007987 introduced in The Structural Urban Form of Washington, DC.

The analysis documents exact reconstruction of the Washington, DC baseline; fine-grained threshold and adjacency sensitivity tests; comparisons of Microsoft Band 1 with municipal building-footprint data in Washington, DC and Philadelphia, PA; and unchanged application of the threshold across six contrasting U.S. cities. Detailed corridor diagnostics examine how I-676 in Philadelphia and I-695 and I-395 in Washington, DC affect native-cell connectivity through surrounding built conditions rather than through a predetermined highway-barrier rule.

The results support retaining SI ≥ 0.007987 as the fixed operational threshold and as a reproducible implementation of a broader empirical operating regime near SI 0.008. They do not establish the threshold as a theoretically unique natural constant. The supplement also distinguishes computational reproducibility from unaffiliated independent replication.

title: It can't happen here: Democratic Backsliding and the Complacency Trap

detail.abstract: We study the interaction of institutions and citizens in a model of democratic backsliding. Greater confidence in institutions' ability to restrain the executive reduces costly vertical restraining. As periods without attempts at backsliding accumulate, institutional confidence increases. This dynamic may generate a complacency trap in which prolonged democratic stability can increase vulnerability to future backsliding. Political heterogeneity and the presence of multiple groups acting as vertical restrainers can further distort the composition of democratic defense and increase the risk of backsliding. Accurate information about institutional restraining capacity and electoral contestability can mitigate the inefficiencies associated with vertical restraining and reduce the risk of backsliding.

detail.abstract: SME credit risk assessment remains costly for lenders, and probability of default (PD) models are the standard instrument for reducing that cost without sacrificing lending quality. Comparing such models on 4,580 SME cases with a 4.3 percent default rate, we find that logistic regression with Weight of Evidence transformation, calibrated Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM and their equal-weight ensemble deliver comparable discrimination once every metric is measured 5-fold out-of-fold with the full pipeline refitted inside each fold. With all five models within 0.04 Gini of one another (0.55 to 0.59), discrimination alone cannot differentiate them; calibration quality and interpretability become the deciding criteria. The study documents three findings the discrimination-focused literature underemphasizes. First, SMOTE resampling in a properly constructed pipeline shapes only intermediate artefacts and leaves every deployed probability unchanged. Second, calibration has a level and a shape requiring different instruments: the natural default rate sets the level, while cross-fitted beta calibration corrects the shape, removing the probability floor imposed by averaged fold-calibrators and moving Random Forest and XGBoost from failing the Hosmer-Lemeshow test to passing it, at a cost of 0.011 Gini. Third, evaluation paths that refit preprocessing on evaluation data inflate results, here by 0.09 Gini for the logistic regression. The article closes with model selection guidance, a rating scale and a validation sequence for institutions balancing performance with supervisory expectations.

title: Internalities and Externalities in the Demand for Flood Protection
affiliations: Pennsylvania State University and Pennsylvania State University

detail.title: Internalities and Externalities in the Demand for Flood Protection
detail.abstract: Levees are chosen by the communities they protect, but household  beliefs about flood risk and levee benefits are frequently wrong. Levees also impose costs on downstream communities by displacing floodwater away from protected areas. We develop a conceptual framework in which each of these features, an internality from misperceived flood risk and an externality from displaced floodwater, appears as a distinct wedge between privately chosen and socially efficient protection. We estimate both wedges using a discrete choice experiment with an embedded randomized information treatment. Households are willing to pay $191 per year for a levee but place no additional value on whether it protects against a 100-, 200-, or 500-year flood, and correcting their beliefs with address-specific risk information does not restore sensitivity to the protection standard. Willingness to pay falls when a levee imposes high downstream damages, implying that households price in roughly 36% of the external cost they create. Combining these estimates with property-level flood exposure for 44,772 at-risk homes, we find that private valuation exceeds social valuation at every protection standard, and the two distortions compound rather than offset. Their composition changes with the standard: the internality accounts for 87% of the gap at the 100-year level ($4.7M versus $0.7M per year) and 62% at the 500-year level ($1.6M versus $0.9M). Since the two wedges arise from different sources, belief correction and downstream pricing are separate policy problems, and which one binds depends on the setting and protection standard.

title: Rethinking Marschak's Maxim: Heckman's Reinterpretation of Marschak

detail.title: Rethinking Marschak's Maxim: Heckman's Reinterpretation of Marschak

detail.abstract: James Heckman's "Marschak's Maxim"-the principle that estimators should be chosen to answer well-posed economic problems with minimal assumptions-is often treated as a concise summary of Jacob Marschak's (1953) classic paper. This note reexamines the relationship between the two, arguing that Heckman's formulation differs in an important respect from Marschak's original argument and asking how this difference arose. Marschak's argument consists of a set of conditional claims: what knowledge of economic structure a policy problem requires depends on the problem itself, and in some cases requires knowledge of whether and how the structure is expected to change under a policy intervention-a concern that Lucas (1976) later formulated more explicitly in terms of the stability of econometric structure under policy changes. This broader information problem is not captured by a single injunction to minimize assumptions. Comparing Heckman's own statements from 2007 through 2010 reveals a progressive narrowing of Marschak's argument. In 2007, Heckman placed Marschak within a lineage concerned with policy-invariant structure; by 2009-2010, Marschak was recast as the source of a minimalist principle in which policy invariance was no longer constitutive of the maxim; in 2010, invariance reappears in the surrounding discussion, but not in the sentence defining the maxim itself. The note therefore interprets "Marschak's Maxim" not as a simple restatement of Marschak's position, but as a reformulation that retains one strand of his argument while leaving another outside its defining formulation.

title: The African Development Paradox: Resource Availability Without Poverty Reduction: A Validation Study of the Recalibrated Blank to Count Ratio (Bcr) as a Programme Implementation Effectiveness Ranking Metric With Beneficiary-Impact Focus

detail.title: The African Development Paradox: Resource Availability Without Poverty Reduction: A Validation Study of the Recalibrated Blank to Count Ratio (Bcr) as a Programme Implementation Effectiveness Ranking Metric With Beneficiary-Impact Focus

detail.abstract: Background: Africa holds 30% of the world's mineral reserves but accounts for less than 3% of global trade, with poverty rising to over 476 million people. Despite 4.9% GDP growth between 2000-2020, the continent fails to convert resource wealth into household resilience, as evidenced by the unmet Millennium Development Goals and floundering Sustainable Development Goals. This study investigates this paradox using Zambia's SCRALA climateresilience project as a primary case study, with comparative analysis from South Africa, Nigeria, Malawi, and Zimbabwe. Method: Using a mixed-methods approach with secondary data from the IMF, World Bank, and national auditors, the study recalibrates the Blank to Count Ratio (BCR); a diagnostic metric distinguishing between COUNT (resources reaching households and building capabilities) and BLANK (resources spent on logistics or training without adoption). Findings: Results show that the paradox is driven by the Triple Diagnostic Failure (spatial, temporal, and compliance blindness), sustained by the Psychostructural Trap. The SCRALA project's baseline BCR is 0.18 (CRITICAL), with 82% of resources tied to institutional capacity rather than direct household impact. However, the Goat Pass-On Mechanism proves that direct interventions work, reaching 9,262 farmers and generating ZMW 4.3 million in sales. Comparative rankings reveal Zambia's CDF at 0.24 (CRITICAL), Nigeria's SDG ranking at 146/166, Malawi's SDG Index at 52.3, and Zimbabwe's conversion score at 19/100 (CRITICAL). Conclusion: The study concludes that the recalibrated BCR provides a validated, near realtime diagnostic tool for ranking programme effectiveness and enabling course correction. It recommends the Individual Demonstration Model where beneficiary ownership, professional support, binary YES/NO verification, and mentorship as a universal blueprint to ensure resources reach households. This approach resolves the development paradox by shifting focus from reporting training completion to verifying adoption and household-level impact, making every programme COUNT rather than BLANK.

detail.abstract:
Objective: Low-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) can modulate cortical activity inducing transient lesions, but effects on cognition vary. Using individualized stimulation targets, we tested whether baseline brain network properties of the stimulated dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) are associated with rTMS effects on executive functioning (EF) and task-related activation.

Methods: In a randomized controlled experiment of 97 healthy adults, individualized DLPFC stimulation targets with the highest multilayer hubness were selected using MRI-derived multilayer networks. Participants received single-session verum (1Hz) or sham rTMS. EF and activation were assessed through a Tower of London (ToL) task during fMRI. Preregistered associations between rTMS-related changes in EF performance were tested. Additionally, pre-post verum versus sham rTMS changes in task-related activation were examined, and a Bayesian region-based analysis (RBA) assessed effects across task-relevant regions.

Results: Baseline multilayer properties were not associated with rTMS-induced change in ToL performance. However, at the most demanding task load, the verum group exhibited a lower decrease in accuracy compared to sham (B = 0.344, p = 0.014). Task-related activation of the target was not significantly altered after verum rTMS, but Bayesian RBA revealed moderate to strong credible evidence (P⁺ = 0.92 – 0.97) for greater decreases in task-related activation in several ROIs in the verum compared to sham.

Conclusion:rTMS-induced changes in EF or activation at the stimulation site were not associated with baseline multilayer properties. However, evidence was found for decrease in activation in task-related brain areas. Additionally, subtle load-dependent effects highlight the complexity of rTMS and warrant further investigation.

title: Heterogeneity in Overnight-versus-Intraday Stock-Return Behavior with Asymmetric Information and 52-week Price Anchoring

detail.abstract: We document substantial cross-sectional heterogeneity in the overnight-intraday return anomaly along two distinct dimensions. First, a stock's asymmetric-information environment, summarized by our composite information-asymmetry metric (INFO-Z), predicts how last month's overnight return is propagated into this month's overnight and intraday returns. Higher INFO-Z stocks exhibit stronger overnight momentum and a stronger intraday cross-reversal. Second, a stock's price relative to its 52-week history, summarized by a composite price-to-52-week-anchor metric (PTA), predicts how last month's intraday return is propagated forward. High PTA stocks exhibit weaker intraday momentum and a weaker overnight cross-reversal. Stocks that were past relative winners are more important in establishing these conditional patterns. Our findings are robust across portfolio sorts, Fama-MacBeth regressions, and control variables motivated by recent explanations, and are stronger with higher investor sentiment. Our INFO-Z results complement the overnight-versus-intraday literature that emphasizes differentially informed agents. Our PTA results introduce the empirical importance of price anchoring in this setting and are consistent with an extrapolative-belief role. Finally, higher INFO-Z stocks earn higher average overnight returns and lower average intraday returns, highlighting the time-of-day dimension of information asymmetry.

September 3, 2026
AS ERISA TURNS 52, NEW REPORT FINDS
AMERICA'S RETIREMENT SYSTEM HAS LEFT

Consumer Policy Center paper updates a landmark 2004 ABA keynote with two

best-interest standard at the point of retirement.
Washington, D.C. – Labor Day 2026 marks 52 years since President Gerald Ford signed the
Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA, Pub. L. 93-406) into law on Labor Day,
September 2, 1974 — a law he said would give workers “much more clearly defined rights to
pension funds and greater assurances that retirement dollars will be there when they are
needed.” A new paper from the Consumer Policy Center, ERISA at 52: Where Is the Employer-
Sponsored System Going, And Who Is It Leaving Behind?, argues that promise remains unmet
for a large and identifiable share of American workers.
The paper, by Dallas L. Salisbury — founding Chief Staff Executive of the Employee Benefit
Research Institute (EBRI) from 1978 to 2015, now a Senior Fellow at the Consumer Policy
Center — updates a keynote he delivered at the American Bar Association's JCEB Symposium
in 2004. Drawing on new data from the Social Security Administration, the Federal Reserve's
Survey of Consumer Finances, Census SIPP, and KFF, it traces what Salisbury calls a “structural
transformation that no one explicitly chose”: the collapse of traditional pension coverage, the
rise of the 401(k) and its persistent adequacy gaps, and growing reliance on Social Security
among older Americans.

detail.abstract: Published employment figures for data center construction come from the industry, from agencies relaying an industry figure, or from unions testifying on projects; this paper could locate no independent series at the metropolitan level. It builds one from federal filings. Labor organisations above a receipts threshold report their membership annually to the Department of Labor under penalty of perjury, and the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers publishes maps of which locals hold inside construction jurisdiction. Joining the two gives an eight-year panel of inside electrical construction membership by metropolitan area for 89 locals. Treatment is a hyperscale campus published by one of four operators in the local's metropolitan area. The median treated local grew 33.7 percent between its 2018 and 2025 filings against 13.2 percent elsewhere, and the regression difference is 25.8 percentage points, 95 percent interval 7.8 to 43.8, clustered on 36 states, with a randomization p-value below 0.001. An event study with local and year fixed effects finds no differential trend in the two pre-period years the panel can see and a divergence significant from 2023, reaching 17.8 log points by 2025. IBEW locals in the same metros that are not on the Inside maps diverged from their own comparison group by less than half as much on medians, and the regression form of that comparison does not survive state fixed effects. The effect is concentrated: removing the five fastest-growing locals leaves 9.0 points and no significance, and removing the four treated metros known to host a federally subsidised semiconductor or battery plant leaves 17.1. Seventeen of the twenty-nine treated locals sit in metros the industry's capacity report does not list in its H2 2025 edition. County employment of nonresidential electrical contractors, from employer tax filings, correlates with the membership series at 0.58 across 86 locals and shows the same treatment contrast independently, 19.6 points, p = 0.003. The paper is descriptive. It has no instrument and no runner-up control, membership is not employment, and within those limits it finds the trade grew where the campuses were built.

title:
Habeas Log: Procedural Traceability for Automated Decisions 
Introducing The Minimum Record and The Inversion of Proof in AI Systems

detail.title:
Habeas Log: Procedural Traceability for Automated Decisions 
Introducing The Minimum Record and The Inversion of Proof in AI Systems

detail.abstract: Automated systems increasingly produce effects on persons who are then expected to challenge those effects without access to the process that produced them. This investigation argues that the decade-long debate over a "right to explanation" has been asking an incomplete question. Legal contestation cannot be made to depend on obtaining an explanation of an opaque model; it can, however, be made to depend on the existence of a record of the act. The paper proposes the Habeas Log: a procedural right, in the genealogy of Habeas Corpus and Habeas Data, to demand the minimum record of an algorithmic act producing legal or comparable effects on a person. It introduces a Minimum Viable Log of five fields (decision hash, model provenance, declared decisional basis, human agency level and recourse endpoint) and paired with a rebuttable evidentiary presumption: where the party exercising algorithmic power cannot produce the record it was required to create, the procedural conditions of accountable decision-making are presumed not to have been met. The paper places the proposal within the explainability and contestability literature, examines it alongside existing protections in the GDPR, the EU AI Act, the Council of Europe Framework Convention, Brazilian and Argentine law, and grounds it in the doctrine of dynamic burdens of proof. Across running cases (an automated credit refusal, an administrative suspension of a social benefit, and a robotaxi halt) it shows what existing law establishes, where the evidentiary gap lies, and how the presence of a minimum record changes the possibility of contestation. A reference implementation and threat model further demonstrate the technical feasibility of generating and verifying the proposed record with standard cryptographic tools, while defining what the record does and does not guarantee.

detail.abstract: Emotional intelligence constitutes a key component of human capital, shaped partially by educational materials. Using machine learning and generative AI tools, we examine emotional content in public-school textbooks and children's literature. A stark mismatch emerges: text exposes children to a broad emotional range, but images overwhelmingly depict happiness and calm, regardless of emotions described in text on the same page. Nearly half of pages show zero overlap between the emotions described in text and those shown in images. This pattern persists across time, contexts, and identities. Household purchases and library inventories suggest content may be endogenously shaped by consumer demand favoring "positive" cover imagery, implying market forces narrow the emotional landscape children encounter.

title: Anchoring Effect of Focal Points in Bargaining: Power and Endowment
affiliations: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics

detail.title: Anchoring Effect of Focal Points in Bargaining: Power and Endowment
detail.abstract: This paper investigates, both theoretically and experimentally, the anchoring effect of focal points in sequential bargaining with varying structures. We design two variants of the Nash bargaining game, each permitting conflict, that encourage players to coordinate via focal points. Specifically, we examine two types: power, defined by expected conflict payoffs, and endowment, which sets the status quo. Experimental results show that players exhibit notable rationality in both their demands and their decisions to back down. Crucially, power exerts a strong anchoring effect, while endowment does not. Strikingly, the opponent’s willingness to back down—interpreted as tacit recognition of the bargainer’s ownership claim—plummets from 65.79% to 12.5% after exposure to  power as the focal point, highlighting the limited role of ownership legitimacy in shaping bargaining outcomes.

detail.abstract: This paper estimates the macrofinancial costs and regional spillovers of the sovereign-bank nexus in Venezuela using two complementary frameworks. First, a Growth-at-Risk (GaR) specification [Adrian et al., 2019] estimates the full conditional distribution of GDP growth as a function of sovereign exposure intensity, revealing that the nexus amplifies downside risk disproportionately: the sovereign stress coefficient at the 5th percentile (β =-84.4) is 1.7 times larger in absolute value than at the median (β =-48.7), implying that the nexus is primarily a tail-risk phenomenon. Second, a Global VAR [Pesaran et al., 2004] embedding Venezuela in a six-country Latin American panel with trade-and-financial-linkage weights and real IMF WEO GDP data (1998-2025) quantifies cross-border transmission. Generalized impulse responses show that a one-standard-deviation Venezuelan GDP shock raises Colombian GDP by 2.0 percentage points at peak and Ecuador by 2.6 pp, with persistence exceeding 10 years. Forecast error variance decomposition attributes 67 percent of Colombian GDP variance and 59 percent of Brazilian GDP variance to Venezuelan shocks at the 10-year horizon. A Bayesian Markov-switching VAR provides complementary regime dating: the posterior probability of the crisis regime exceeds 0.90 for the entire 2010-2023 sample, confirming that Venezuela experienced a single, protracted structural break rather than episodic recessions. A smooth-transition VAR (STVAR) identifies 301 percent year-on-year inflation as the dollarization threshold above which oil-price shocks are amplified tenfold in the sovereign-bank transmission channel. The combined evidence establishes the Venezuelan nexus as the most extreme case in the emerging-market literature and demonstrates that its costs propagate well beyond Venezuelan borders.

detail.abstract: Recent debates regarding the relative efficiency of the hybrid and pure platform modes have become central in platform economics. This paper investigates the effect of the platform mode in a setting where downstream sellers on the platform purchase products from an upstream manufacturer before competing in quantities. The choice between the hybrid and pure platform modes alters the upstream manufacturer's pricing incentives and, in turn, affects total market quantity and welfare. I derive the conditions under which the hybrid platform mode yields a higher, lower, or equal total quantity compared to the pure platform mode. The key determinant is the modularity of demand, which depends on the elasticity of marginal revenue. These results highlight that platform regulation should jointly consider demand structure, upstream pricing behavior, and market structure.

detail.abstract: In May 2025, China's fund regulator mandated a performance-fee schedule for newly issued active equity funds with an unusual geometry: the penalty for trailing the benchmark by three percentage points is twice the reward for beating it by six, and the fee settles lot by lot over each investor's own holding window. We model such penalty-heavy, vintage-contingent contracts. The bounded, penalty-tilted schedule taxes tracking variance: managers below a skill threshold optimally closet-index, and within the evaluation year the risk response is non-monotone, with gambling zones near the downgrade and upgrade lines and an incentive dead zone in deeper losses, where performance-linked marginal incentives decay toward zero. Lot-by-lot settlement makes money age a state variable: young lots face a penalty-tilted lottery, while window averaging launders luck out of maturing lots at an exponential rate. Under the partial mandate, fund companies assign floating contracts to their strongest managers, an endorsement reversal visible in the first cohort's appointment data. The fee schedule is interpretable as a compromise among three documented regulatory concerns: punishing persistent failure, limiting reward-induced gambling, and keeping the active industry viable. First-year evidence from the inaugural cohort is suggestive.

detail.abstract: This paper extends the sovereign-bank nexus analysis of Marcano (2026a) along five structural dimensions. First, I develop a two-period model of financial repression with a binding fiscal need constraint, deriving three equilibrium concepts-Stackelberg, Nash, and Ramsey-that characterize the Venezuelan banking system's sovereign exposure. The fiscal need parameter F is calibrated from independent fiscal data (IMF Article IV primary deficits), and the model predicts observed exposure ratios out of sample with errors of +7.8, +1.9, and-4.2 percentage points for 2017, 2020, and 2023 respectively. The welfare cost of financial repression is 54.6% of Ramsey output in consumptionequivalent units. Second, Toda-Yamamoto Granger causality tests-robust to the integration order of the series and validated by ADF/KPSS stationarity diagnostics-on quarterly data sourced from OPEC, IMF IFS, and BCV reveal that the reserve requirement (encaje) Granger-causes sovereign exposure (p < 0.001), with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals confirming significance. Third, a crosscountry counterfactual against 39 EMDEs using World Bank GFDD 2023-vintage data documents excess nexus of 34.5-43.6 pp above the petro-EMDE median, with bootstrap 95% CIs. Fourth, currency mismatch risk is quantified using SUDEBAN-sourced FX decomposition with time-varying deposit-to-asset ratios, finding NOP/Equity of-187.5% by December 2020, with VaR uncertainty bands from the volatility estimation window. Fifth, composition sensitivity and robustness checks-alternative interpolation methods, alternative exposure definitions, subsample stability, and Cornish-Fisher VaR-confirm the baseline findings.

detail.abstract: This paper constructs the first comprehensive measure of the sovereign-bank nexus in Venezuela using primary-source regulatory data from SUDEBAN (Superintendencia de las Instituciones del Sector Bancario) for three cross-sections: December 2017, December 2020, and December 2023. I define sovereign exposure as the sum of four components: required reserves at the BCV (encaje), BCV securities (títulos), Treasury bonds (DPN/TIF), and other state obligations including PDVSA. Quarterly time series of the exposure ratio are constructed via Denton (1971) benchmarking, using monthly oil production as the interpolation indicator. The results reveal that Venezuelan banks' sovereign exposure peaked at 72.4% of total assets in December 2020, declined to 44.2% by December 2023, and has stabilized at that level through mid-2026. At its peak, sovereign exposure represented 312% of banking system equity, creating a structural vulnerability in which a moderate sovereign haircut would render the entire banking system insolvent. Stress-test scenarios with inflation-implied haircuts of 28-64% generate capital shortfalls ranging from zero to 29% of GDP, depending on the macroeconomic scenario. These findings quantify the fiscal contingency embedded in the Venezuelan sovereign-bank nexus and provide a data foundation for the structural model developed in the companion paper (Marcano, 2026b).

title: When Agency Becomes Abundant: What Becomes Scarce in an Economy of AI Agents? A Theory of Consequential Agency Conversion, Scarcity Frontiers, and Endogenous Authority

detail.title: When Agency Becomes Abundant: What Becomes Scarce in an Economy of AI Agents? A Theory of Consequential Agency Conversion, Scarcity Frontiers, and Endogenous Authority

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this study because it is theoretical and computational in nature and involved no human participants, patient data, or identifiable personal information.

detail.abstract:
What becomes scarce when intelligent agency itself becomes abundant?
As AI agents become cheaper to replicate, coordinate, and deploy, the economically binding constraint may shift away from generic computational capability toward the institutional channels that convert potential action into accepted consequence. This paper develops a formal theory of that transition.

The framework separates potential synthetic agency from attempted, authorized, admitted, and realized action, and defines an agency-conversion ratio that identifies where consequential capacity is lost. It then models consequential capacity and legitimate risk-bearing authority as endogenous supplies rather than fixed bottlenecks. This makes it possible to ask a stricter question than whether a bottleneck appears: whether it persists after investment, institutional entry, competition, and bypass responses.

The paper derives benchmark equilibrium conditions, develops an authority-persistence boundary, and links system-level scarcity to principal-level conversion through heterogeneous exposure. It also distinguishes genuine consequential scarcity from gateway market power, resource cost, and ordinary congestion, and introduces welfare and allocation constraints so that restricted conversion is not automatically treated as social failure.

The central claim is deliberately conditional. The framework does not predict that an “authority economy” must emerge. Instead, it specifies the circumstances under which downstream constraints can become economically dominant—and the conditions under which the theory should collapse back into standard explanations based on congestion, wealth, platforms, delegation, or property rights.

The paper therefore offers a falsifiable research programme for studying how scalable AI agency may interact with finite institutional capacity in future economies.ai. agent.

detail.abstract: In May 2025, China's fund regulator mandated a performance-fee schedule for newly issued active equity funds with an unusual geometry: the penalty for trailing the benchmark by three percentage points is twice the reward for beating it by six, and the fee settles lot by lot over each investor's own holding window. We model such penalty-heavy, vintage-contingent contracts. The bounded, penalty-tilted schedule taxes tracking variance: managers below a skill threshold optimally closet-index, and within the evaluation year the risk response is non-monotone, with gambling zones near the downgrade and upgrade lines and an incentive dead zone in deeper losses, where performance-linked marginal incentives decay toward zero. Lot-by-lot settlement makes money age a state variable: young lots face a penalty-tilted lottery, while window averaging launders luck out of maturing lots at an exponential rate. Under the partial mandate, fund companies assign floating contracts to their strongest managers, an endorsement reversal visible in the first cohort's appointment data. The fee schedule is interpretable as a compromise among three documented regulatory concerns: punishing persistent failure, limiting reward-induced gambling, and keeping the active industry viable. First-year evidence from the inaugural cohort is suggestive.

title:

A Layered Diagnostic Framework for Simulated Multi-agent Pricing Markets

detail.abstract:
Algorithmic pricing systems operating in repeated market environments can produce harmful outcomes: high prices, sticky allocation, unserved demand, and role-level displacement. These outcomes are often read as collusion, but similar surfaces can arise from capacity shortage, consumer switching friction, reward-scale mismatch, or blocked outside options. Treating these mechanisms as equivalent leads to misdiagnosis and misguided intervention. 

      We introduce Strategic Automata Lab, a simulation-based layered diagnostic framework for repeated multi-agent pricing games. The framework separates market simulation, behavioral regime discovery, counterfactual repair, Markov transition topology, heuristic friction scoring, outside-option screening, and observable-only export preparation. Its outputs are descriptive diagnostic signatures under model assumptions, not legal findings. 
 
      The main simulation result is a shortage-displacement double dissociation. In the welfarebackground balanced asymmetric pairing cells, severe shortage keeps aggregate failure high (0.603) while displacement stays near zero (0.013); proxy-lock cells show the reverse pattern, with displacement 0.350 at moderate aggregate failure 0.129. The magnitude is background-dependent, and a seed-level extract of the myopic-background grid confirms the same directional separation with dispersion (balanced proxy-lock vs. shortage: displacement 0.142 ± 0.127 vs. 0.004 ± 0.001; failure 0.120 ± 0.029 vs. 0.606 ± 0.009). A focused uncertainty-penalty sweep also separates stable learning from lock-in-like dynamics: between 𝜆 = 3.0 and 𝜆 = 3.5, mean final Nash gap rises from 79.867 to 579.967 and mean lock-in inefficiency rises from 0.089 to 0.681. 

      External marketplace runs are feasibility audits only. The current evidence is simulationbased; real-world diagnostic accuracy and legal classification remain future validation tasks.

title: Clothes as Human Infrastructure: Materials, Functions, Culture, Sustainability, and Intelligent Futures

detail.title: Clothes as Human Infrastructure: Materials, Functions, Culture, Sustainability, and Intelligent Futures

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or non-financial interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This article is a review and does not involve human participants, animals or identifiable personal data.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this review.

detail.abstract: Clothing is often discussed as fashion, yet it is more accurately understood as a form of human infrastructure that connects the body to climate, culture, technology, labour and the biosphere. This integrative review develops a systems account of clothes across six linked domains: physiological protection and comfort; material and manufacturing science; identity and social meaning; global production and work; environmental life-cycle performance; and intelligent or adaptive textiles. The review synthesizes peer-reviewed literature and authoritative institutional reports identified through targeted searches of publisher and public-agency databases. Global fibre production reached approximately 132 million tonnes in 2024, with polyester accounting for about 59% and cotton about 19%, illustrating the continuing dominance of high-volume fibre systems and the growing material throughput of apparel. Environmental burdens arise at different stages: feedstock and fibre cultivation or synthesis, wet processing, garment assembly, logistics, laundering and drying, microfibre release, and end-of-life loss. No fibre is universally superior across climate, water, land, toxicity, durability and recyclability indicators; therefore, fibre substitution alone is insufficient. The most robust cross-cutting strategy is to deliver more safe and valued service from fewer garments through fit, quality, durability, repairability, care optimization, reuse and credible recovery systems. Social performance is equally central because clothing supply chains combine economic opportunity with persistent risks related to wages, excessive hours, chemical exposure, building safety and unequal bargaining power. Smart textiles may expand clothing into continuous sensing, thermal management and human-machine interaction, but they also introduce new problems of power, privacy, wash durability, repair and electronic waste. The paper proposes a nested clothing-systems framework and a preferred intervention hierarchy—avoid, reduce, extend, reuse, recycle and controlled disposal. It concludes that the future of clothing should be evaluated not by novelty or unit price alone, but by inclusive human service per unit of material, energy, ecological pressure and labour risk.

title: Innovation Without Adoption: Clean Technology Adoption and Sustainable Growth
affiliations: University of Wisconsin - Milwaukee - Department of Economics

detail.title: Innovation Without Adoption: Clean Technology Adoption and Sustainable Growth
detail.abstract: This paper studies the incentives to adopt existing clean technologies in an overlapping generations endogenous growth model. I show that even when technologies are available, finitely-lived generations under-adopt clean technologies because they fail to internalize the future environmental benefits of adoption. In addition to harming environmental quality, this intergenerational under-adoption of clean technologies can dampen long-run economic growth. This implies that the mere supply of technological progress is insufficient to ensure long-run economic growth when these technologies are under adopted. These results support public policies that encourage the adoption of clean technologies alongside policies that foster ongoing innovation.

detail.abstract: This paper aims to reconcile two measures of return on shareholders’ capital: on one hand, the expected return arising from the use of the Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM), and on the other, the realized Return on Equity (ROE) as an accounting measure of capital efficiency. Both metrics ultimately refer to the same underlying variable—the cost of equity Ke—yet they are seldom analyzed jointly in the literature. Using quarterly fundamental data for all S&P 500 constituents from 1996 to 2025, we construct aggregate earnings yields and book ROE series and compare them against realized index-level total returns. Our hypothesis is that, over sufficiently long horizons, both indicators should converge, since expected returns should equal realized returns when expectations are fulfilled on average. We find that the long-run annualized S&P 500 total return (10.1%) lies between the average aggregate earnings yield (4.3%) and the average book ROE (13.3%), with the wedge fully explained by the Price-to-Book ratio and the earnings growth rate through the Gordon Growth Model identity E(R) = (ROE − g)/(P/B) + g. detail.abstract: Electronic price impact is commonly modeled as a function of trade sign, volume, order-flow imbalance, volatility, and available depth. Yet aggressive flows of comparable size and direction can produce sharply different price responses across time, instruments, and market regimes. This paper develops a state-based theory of Market Susceptibility and Structural Stiffness, proposing that price response depends not only on the pressure applied to an electronic market but also on the evolving structural condition through which that pressure propagates. Market susceptibility is defined as the conditional price displacement associated with an incremental unit of directional pressure given the prevailing configuration of liquidity commitment, structural mass, queue geometry, withdrawal, replenishment, spread, volatility, and recent state history. Structural stiffness denotes the corresponding capacity of that state to resist displacement. Both are empirical response constructs, not literal physical constants. The framework distinguishes static thinness from dynamic susceptibility. A book may be shallow yet resistant because replenishment is rapid and persistent, or visually deep yet highly susceptible because displayed quantity is transient, commitment is deteriorating, and structural support is discontinuous.

detail.abstract: This paper asks whether rolling roughness estimates that label volatility states also rank the shape of near-term tail variation. The design freezes the January 2020-July 2026 Binance BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT tape, 9,560 six-hour origins per contract, and the three functionals used in companion work. Forward 8-hour and 24-hour outcomes are reconstructed from one-minute sufficient statistics. At eight hours, a one-standard-deviation increase in Ĥᴵ is ⱽ associated with 0.186 log points more realized quarticity in Bitcoin and 0.166 in Ether; the corresponding Ĥᴾᴬ effects are 0.177 and 0.157. Origin-level 14-day block-cluster inference preserves all four effects, whereas Ĥᴾ remains null. ⱽ The accounting identity log RQ = 2 log RV + log NRQ locates the association: it loads through realized-variance scale. Log normalized quarticity, the raw bipower-residual share, and a conservative RQ-scaled significance-filtered residual all satisfy prespecified equivalence tests. title: Market for Information: Sequential Provision of Information

detail.abstract: I study the design of markets for information when the seller is profit-motivated rather than persuasion-motivated. I propose a simple analytical tool to characterize the optimal information design problem of such a seller and apply it to study two practices that respond to the classical challenges of selling information identified by Arrow (1962). First, the common "paywall" practice of providing free preview information has no value to the seller when the buyer has standard decision-theoretic preferences, but it strictly increases profit when the buyer has some belief-dependent preferences. Second, when the seller faces multiple buyers whose actions are publicly observable, a deliberate sequential sale protocol can mitigate the profit loss from information spillover. I characterize the optimal order of approach, the optimal market coverage, and the optimal experiment design. I also show that information spillover, typically a restriction on the seller, can in fact become an opportunity when buyers are averse to intermediate posteriors.

detail.title: Fractals and their Applications

detail.abstract:
This project investigates whether fractal and multifractal methods provide a more informative description of complex systems than classical linear, Gaussian, and random-walk models. The main focus is financial-market dynamics, with particular attention to cryptocurrencies, bond markets, and commodities, while also situating fractal geometry within the broader study of natural systems, nonlinear dynamics, and deterministic chaos. 

The study combines theoretical review with empirical case studies. Fractal geometry, the Hurst exponent, fractional Brownian motion, deterministic chaos, and multifractal analysis are used to examine persistence, scale dependence, and heterogeneous structure. Empirical illustrations are developed using Bitcoin and silver price data, including rescaled range analysis, rollingwindow Hurst exponent estimation, detrended fluctuation analysis, and multifractal diagnostics. Evidence from the literature is also used to compare these findings with fractal and multifractal behaviour in bond markets, gold, oil, biological systems, geophysical structures, technology, medicine, and data science. 

The results show that fractal behaviour is not confined to a single asset class or application area. Bitcoin exhibits persistent, regime-dependent scaling behaviour, while silver displays timevarying persistence and multifractal structure. Bond-market evidence also supports the presence of long-range dependence and multifractality, particularly in interest-rate and yield dynamics. Across these examples, fractal methods reveal structure that is often missed by classical models based on independence, normality, and short-memory assumptions. The project therefore argues that fractal and multifractal analysis should be understood primarily as diagnostic tools for identifying persistence, heterogeneity, volatility clustering, and scale-dependent behaviour in complex systems. Overall, the findings support the use of fractal frameworks as a bridge between financial modelling, nonlinear dynamics, and broader scientific descriptions of complexity.

detail.abstract: Court digitalisation is often framed through large infrastructure projects, yet everyday court administration is also burdened by smaller, repetitive information failures: locating the correct office, identifying the required form, finding an approved instruction, or resolving a recurring technical issue. These interruptions consume staff time, fragment attention and reproduce knowledge informally. This policy brief presents THEMIS, a governance-first proposal for a controlled artificial-intelligence help desk at the Thessaloniki Courthouse. The model combines a public self-service kiosk with an authenticated internal application for judicial staff. Both interfaces draw on a curated knowledge base, but they operate with different content and access rights. The system is deliberately excluded from case files, case-specific information, legal advice, adjudication, outcome prediction and any decision assigned to a judicial or administrative authority. Its technical logic is retrieval-augmented generation with visible sources, content ownership, version control, abstention and human escalation. The proposal is grounded in an exploratory survey of 264 Greek judicial employees conducted in 2025, while recognising the limits of a voluntary, self-selected sample. It recommends a three-month, noexternal-cost preparation stage before procurement, followed-only if the evidence supports continuation-by a bounded twelve-month pilot with baseline measurement, security testing and independent evaluation. The central claim is that trustworthy AI in court administration begins with information governance, not model acquisition.

title: Mapping the Dollarisation and De-dollarisation Research Field, 1991-2026: Intellectual Structure, Life-Cycle Dynamics and Emerging Research Fronts

detail.abstract: The renewed policy salience of currency sovereignty has generated a rapidly expanding scholarship whose structure remains poorly charted. This study maps the intellectual and social architecture of dollarisation and de-dollarisation research through a bibliometric analysis of 769 documents indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection between 1991 and 2026, retrieved on 5 September 2026 and analysed using BiblioSpy. Performance indicators, source and author productivity, institutional contribution, citation trajectories and logistic life-cycle models are reported, and every headline indicator is independently recomputed from the raw export. The corpus has accumulated 8,281 citations (h = 43; g = 64; e = 39.37), is led by the Journal of International Money and Finance (33 documents) and the International Monetary Fund (26 documents), and is markedly single-authored (42.7 per cent). Three results qualify the conventional reading of such data. First, the headline annual growth rate of 17.98 per cent is a cumulative-series statistic; annual output has grown at 10.60 per cent, and the logistic model's forecast of post-2024 decline is contradicted by observed output, which exceeds the fitted peak by roughly two-thirds. Second, the apparent post-2020 collapse in citations per publication is a joint artefact of the citation window and a compositional shift towards emerging-index and bookform outlets, not a decline in quality. Third, de-dollarisation is not a mature theme but a research front formed almost entirely after 2020: all documents addressing BRICS, 95 per cent of those addressing digital currencies and 94 per cent of those addressing sanctions appear in 2021-2026. The field is expanding and reorienting rather than saturating.

detail.abstract:
Classical monetary theory treats the source of monetary value as sovereign issuance, aggregate demand, or currency competition , but does not account for the structural role of verified human networks as an independent monetary substrate. This paper addresses that gap by introducing a formal mathematical model, the Network-Based Monetary Theory (NBMT), which proposes that under conditions of advancing digitization and geopolitical fragmentation, the structural properties of verified human networks , network scale, verified participation, economic activity density, tokenized asset depth, and external centralization risk , become determinants of monetary value independent of sovereign issuance.

The model derives two formal instruments: the Network Sovereignty Index (V_s), a dimensionless comparative measure of network monetary legitimacy computed from four observable parameters (ρ_v, α_e, σ_r, R_ext); and the Unit Exchange Value (P_unit), integrating Metcalfe's network law with Fisher's equation of exchange via a structural transfer function V = f(V_s). 

Five falsifiable hypotheses are ordered from internal network architecture (H1–H3) to external institutional interaction (H4–H5), with all eight partial derivatives verified for sign consistency. An illustrative empirical application across five anonymized network archetypes (Part XIII) demonstrates computational tractability and produces four findings directionally consistent with the model's predictions: R_ext centralization suppresses V_s regardless of other variables; verified identity without economic activity produces insufficient network sovereignty; tokenized assets lower the critical mass threshold; and no current network archetype meets the transition condition , consistent with NBMT's projected 2035 horizon. The endogeneity problem in the V_s , α_e relationship is addressed through a lagged variable specification consistent with Arellano-Bond GMM practice, with Granger causality testing identified as the required next empirical step. 

The model is presented as a research program open to testing, refutation, and development , not as an established monetary law.

detail.abstract: Using 0DTE SPX options, I show that the option-implied uncertainty of the prospective shock accumulates rather than resolves before scheduled FOMC announcements. The implied uncertainty monotonically rises from 10:00 ET to the 14:00 ET release and largely collapses at the announcement. Both the level and the accumulation of the implied uncertainty strongly forecast realized volatility in any window after the announcement time, but not prior to it. The implied skewness is uniformly negative, varies little, and does not predict returns. Immediately after the introduction of Wednesday-expiring 0DTE options, the pre-announcement drift documented in the literature disappears, indicating that the drift reflected compensation for previously unobservable event uncertainty. The same accumulation-and-release pattern appears around FOMC Minutes and the closing auction, scaled to their information content. The 0DTE option market prices any regularly anticipated concentration of price discovery in the same accumulating fashion, whether macroeconomic or microstructural.

detail.abstract:
This paper investigates whether Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) disclosures by South African mining corporations listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) act as genuine mechanisms for downside risk mitigation or function primarily as greenwashing signals. Traditional empirical studies on JSE mining equities often rely on ordinary least squares correlations that suffer from endogeneity and omitted variable bias. To overcome these limitations, we implement a Causal Bayesian Structural framework using PyMC to isolate the causal effect of ESG transparency on firm-level downside risk-specifically Value at Risk (VaR) and Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR)-while explicitly accounting for parameter uncertainty. Using 39,682 daily observations of 18 JSE mining tickers from 2016-2024, posterior distributions confirm a negative relationship between verified ESG intensity and downside risk (β esg ≈-1.85). Counterfactual analysis shows greenwashing yields minimal VaR protection compared to substantive operational changes. 

Furthermore, this study contributes to sustainability finance literature by bridging causal inference and Bayesian uncertainty quantification for the South African market. The framework distinguishes symbolic disclosure from operational substance, providing regulators, investors, and scholars with a probabilistic tool to audit ESG credibility under King IV and ESG rating divergence.

title: Innovation vs. Regulatory Intervention: The Cost of Change

detail.abstract: The relationship between regulation and innovation is commonly framed as a debate between two competing views. One argues that regulation suppresses innovation by imposing costs and constraining experimentation. The other maintains that well-designed regulation enables innovation by creating trust, certainty, and functioning markets. This paper argues that both perspectives overlook a more fundamental variable: the rate of regulatory change itself. Drawing on law and economics, policy uncertainty literature, and German constitutional principles of legal certainty, the paper develops the concept of regulatory churn. Every regulatory change, regardless of whether it increases or decreases regulatory burdens, must be discovered, interpreted, and implemented at cost. These transition costs are independent of the substantive quality of the change. The paper identifies three characteristics that make regulatory churn particularly harmful to innovation: asymmetry, indeterminacy, and cumulativeness. It argues that frequent regulatory modification disproportionately affects smaller firms, increases uncertainty, and creates cumulative burdens that are often overlooked in impact assessments. Innovation policy should therefore evaluate not only the content of regulation, but also the costs generated by regulatory change itself.
