detail.abstract: The paper examines why climate-related information does not consistently become a traceable signal in corporate bond prices, contracts, and secondary-market resilience. It defines transmission adequacy as the ability to connect a material exposure to the correct legal obligor, align it with the information date and financial horizon, document its treatment by credit intermediaries, and observe it in financing and stress-state indicators. A structured critical review of 40 verified academic and institutional sources organizes evidence around five links: disclosure, exposure measurement, pricing and contract design, credit intermediation, and market resilience. The synthesis identifies five corresponding frictions-legal-entity and asset-location mismatch, information-date and horizon misalignment, measurement non-comparability, absorption by ratings, guarantees and ownership, and limited price discovery in thinly traded bonds. For China, the article proposes Module 1, an issuer-emitter-bond map; Module 2, bond-relevant climate disclosure; Module 3, transparent intermediary treatment; Module 4, a climate-credit stress dashboard; and Module 5, pre-specified pilots and proportional scaling. These modules target traceability rather than an administratively imposed premium and are paired with burden safeguards, implementation metrics and failure interpretations.

title: Data Thickets: Compound IP Barriers and the Enclosure of Algorithmic Infrastructure

detail.title: Data Thickets: Compound IP Barriers and the Enclosure of Algorithmic Infrastructure

detail.abstract: Algorithms set the rent for three million apartments, determine credit scores used in 90% of U.S. lending decisions, and reprice insurance claims worth billions of dollars annually. The enforcement debate over these systems has focused on conduct-whether coordination through a shared algorithm constitutes a Sherman Act violation. This Note identifies a structural problem the conduct debate has overlooked. The algorithmic systems at the center of every major enforcement action are concentrated infrastructure, and that infrastructure is being enclosed behind compound IP barriers: overlapping proprietary data relationships, patent portfolios, trade secret protections, compute concentration, and regulatory entrenchment operating simultaneously. Each barrier type has generated its own doctrinal literature. No existing framework analyzes their interaction. This Note introduces the compound barrier framework and coins the term "data thicket" to describe overlapping proprietary data-sharing relationships that foreclose competitive entry through the same structural mechanics Carl Shapiro identified in patent thickets. Drawing on empirical evidence from three markets-multifamily rental housing (RealPage), consumer credit scoring (FICO), and frontier AI-the Note documents how data thickets, patent thickets, trade secret opacity, compute concentration, and regulatory moats reinforce one another, producing structural foreclosure that exceeds the sum of the individual barriers. FICO's credit scoring market provides the paradigm case: two decades of alternative availability, active regulatory liberalization, and a 1,500% price increase have produced zero market share displacement-a result no singlebarrier framework can explain.

detail.abstract:
Background: It is unclear whether differential attrition between trial arms threatens the validity, representativeness, and results of newer glucose-lowering drug trials. We assessed whether there is differential attrition by estimating the effects of treatment, age, and sex-related differences in arm-level attrition and exploring implications for treatment effect estimates.

Methods: Using an existing systematic review (MEDLINE, Embase, and US/Chinese trial registries to November 2022; updated August 2024), we modelled attrition in a Bayesian network meta-analysis incorporating aggregate and individual participant data (IPD), and an IPD network meta-regression of treatment, age, sex, and interactions. We assessed the impact of differential attrition in exploratory analyses by imputing arm-level HbA1c non-completer outcomes under different assumptions.

Findings: We included 364 trials (92 with IPD; 202,856 participants; mean age, 56·9 years [SD, 9·8]; 45·6% female; 14·3% attrition). Sex was not associated with attrition. Versus placebo, attrition was lower for DPP4 and SGLT2 inhibitors (odds ratio [OR], 0·71 [95% credible intervals 0·66–0·76] and 0·69 [0·63–0·76]), and similar for GLP1 receptor agonists (0·93 [0·85–1·02]). Attrition decreased with age for placebo (OR-per-decade, 0·89 [0·85–0·92]) and DPP4 inhibitors (0·90 [0·85–0·95]). Age-attrition associations were null for GLP1 receptor agonists (0·97 [0·91–1·03]) and SGLT2 inhibitors (1·06 [0·99–1·13]). Assumptions about non-completer HbA1c altered the magnitude, but not direction, of estimated treatment effects.

Interpretation: Attrition varied by treatment class and age. Treatment conclusions were robust to differential assumptions about non-completer outcomes. Nevertheless, differential attrition was evident and arm-level differences varied with age.

title: ImputeBench: Benchmarking Single Imputation Methods
affiliations: German Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases (DZNE), German Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases (DZNE), German Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases (DZNE), German Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases (DZNE) and German Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases (DZNE)

detail.title: ImputeBench: Benchmarking Single Imputation Methods
detail.abstract: ​Biomedical data often contain missing values and in many applications missing value imputation (MVI) is an important part of the data analysis work-flow. However, the performance of MVI methods depends on details of the joint distribution of data and missingness patterns that are typically unknown in practice, making an a priori choice of MVI method challenging. Furthermore, technical assumptions underlying MVI methods can be hard to directly verify in practice. Motivated by these issues, in this paper, we propose an approach for the context-specific selection of MVI methods. Due to the fact that diﬀerent methods may work well in diﬀerent cases we argue for a move away from a “one size fits all” view and put forward in this paper a standardized, empirical approach in which MVI methods are benchmarked in the specific context of a problem of interest. We connect our work to the large body of MVI research, along the way refining definitions of missing at random and missing not at random and providing a detailed review of existing work on benchmarking. Our approach can be tailored to reflect specific assumptions on missingness patterns, allowing for application in diverse applied problems. Furthermore, in addition to using real data, we study benchmarking via data simulation spanning a broad range of properties, such as latent factors, non-linearity and multi-modality, with interpretable simulation parameters that are amenable to user specification. The approaches we propose can be used to (i) select an MVI method for a given data set or (ii) benchmark a novel MVI method across a range of regimes. Alongside the general protocol, we provide a specific, reproducible implementation (in the R-package ImputeBench, available under github.com/richterrob/ImputeBench) that gives users a ready-to-use tool for MVI selection and assessment. We illustrate the use of ImputeBench to study the behaviour of a range of existing imputation methods (k-nn, soft impute, missForest, MICE) in the context of real data from an ongoing large-scale population-level study.

detail.abstract: This research examines the economic logic underpinning skilled migration policies adopted by right-wing governments, exploring a central paradox: how administrations that campaign on restrictive immigration simultaneously pursue active recruitment of highly educated foreign workers. The analysis synthesizes evidence from multiple national contexts-Canada, Germany, Sweden, Australia, and the United Kingdom-to demonstrate that skilled migration has become a cornerstone of economic strategy even under right-wing governance, driven by demographic pressures, fiscal sustainability concerns, and productivity imperatives. The economic justification rests on three pillars. First, younger, highly educated immigrants generate substantial net fiscal surpluses, with long-term projections indicating significant positive effects on public finances. Second, ageing populations and labour shortages in critical sectors-particularly healthcare, technology, and engineering-create structural dependencies on foreign talent that transcend political ideology. Third, skills-based systems are framed as instruments of economic nation-building, selecting immigrants who embody productive citizenship while distinguishing them from less-welcome categories. However, this economic rationality operates within a politically constrained environment. Restrictive rhetoric and hostile policies exert a repulsive effect on highly skilled immigrants, lowering the average educational attainment of migrant inflows and creating a self-reinforcing cycle: anti-immigrant sentiment deters skilled workers, which in turn fuels further populist support. This dynamic is evident across multiple cases where restrictive measures have threatened innovation sectors and undermined recruitment efforts. The research identifies a fundamental tension in rightwing approaches to skilled migration: the coexistence of neoliberal economic logic-which treats migrants as human capital optimising fiscal outcomes-with nationalist identity politics that view immigration as culturally threatening. This tension manifests in policy contradictions, such as facilitating skilled entry while restricting pathways to citizenship, or pursuing bilateral recruitment agreements while maintaining hostile border regimes. The findings suggest that the economic justification for skilled migration under right-wing governments reveals deeper contradictions within contemporary conservative governance, where economic necessity and political identity remain in persistent tension.

detail.abstract: Anomalous cross-field electron transport in closed-drift configurations exceeds the classical collisional prediction by one to two orders of magnitude and has resisted first-principles prediction for five decades. The mechanism is not in doubt; what is absent is a closure from instability drive to saturated transport coefficient. This paper asks a prior question, which linear theory can answer: under what conditions is the drift-driven channel accessible at all. A kinetic dispersion relation for magnetised drifting electrons and unmagnetised ions is solved numerically for the field at which its maximum growth rate changes sign. Instability at perpendicular propagation is found to occupy narrow discrete bands whose centres follow an analytic resonance condition; the bands are narrower than conventional grid spacings, and six numerical failure modes are identified, five of which produce a spurious classification of stability. Applied to a near-isothermal sodium gap at 0.33 V, the collisionless calculation admits a growing root at every accessible field, but ceases to be self-consistent above 26 mT where the electron-neutral collision frequency exceeds the growth rate. With collisions retained the growth rate crosses zero at 25.45 ± 0.10 mT, and no competing unstable harmonic is found up to the transit-based ion magnetisation bound of 66 mT. The boundary scales as the neutral density to the power-0.140. Three fields are distinguished: the resonant-scale crossing at which the long-wavelength ordering fails, the field at which the eigenvalue changes sign, and the field at which macroscopic transport is suppressed, which this work does not determine.

detail.abstract: Nuclear fusion has long been jokingly referred to as the energy source that is "always 50 years away." The root of this curse lies not in the lag of any single technology, but in the deep misalignment of multiple timescales: technology iteration cycles (5-10 years), infrastructure construction cycles (10-20 years), investment return cycles (20-30 years), and climate target cycles (2030/2050 milestones). In 2026, global fusion reached a historic inflection point: China's EAST device achieved 1,066 seconds of steady-state long-pulse high-confinement plasma operation at 100 million degrees Celsius (cumulative injected energy of 3.05 GJ); the ITER project's core component-the divertor-completed full development, with the Chinese consortium undertaking the world's first reactor-scale divertor integration; US-based CFS's SPARC device is over 75% complete, targeting net energy gain (Q > 1) by 2027; global fusion industry annual funding reached USD 4.48 billion, with cumulative funding of USD 14.242 billion and over 16,000 employees. Yet Nature concurrently reported that 46 fusion companies face "overly optimistic" timelines, and Nature Energy research warned that fusion experience rates are only 2%-8%, far below industry assumptions of 8%-20% Based on the complete theoretical system of Prim-Lex Theory (Economic Climatology)—the Fivefold Prim-Fire (Physical Prim-Fire at the joule scale, Animal Prim-Fire of NADH/NAD⁺ metabolic coherence, Plant Prim-Fire of photosynthetic quantum efficiency, Prim-Fire of Mind of neuronal coherence, and Earth-System Intelligence-Coherence Prim-Fire at the planetary scale), the Three-Tier GC⁴A Constraints, the Five-Element Dynamic Coupling Equations, the Eight-Dimensional Framework, and the Prim-Nexus Guidance—this paper introduces, for the first time, nuclear fusion commercialization into the mathematical expression of the complexified unified field Ψ𝑘𝑘 = 𝐴𝐴𝑘𝑘𝑒𝑒𝑖𝑖𝜃𝜃𝑘𝑘. This paper focuses on applying the Seven Luminaires·Seven Rhythms model (Kuramoto coupled-oscillator synchronization theory) to coordinate the phase differences of seven temporal rhythms, and applying the CLL phase-transition early warning model to identify "critical windows." Using the progress of ITER, SPARC, EAST, BEST, and other projects as empirical anchors, the research shows that the current Seven Luminaires synchronization degree of global fusion commercialization is 𝜎𝜎Seven Luminaires, Fusion ≈ 0.35–0.50, indicating severe desynchronization; the CLL phase-transition early warning index is ΨCLL, Fusion ≈ 1.35, indicating a high phase-transition risk zone. This paper proposes the "Fusion Temporal Coherent State" as a unified criterion for assessing the health of the fusion commercialization process, providing a quantifiable, programmable, and auditable mathematical language and governance tool for the transition of global fusion energy from "technology validation" to "grid-connected power generation."

title: Interpretable Health-state Estimation of Hydrogen-Fueled Solid Oxide Fuel Cells under Aviation Dynamic Environments
affiliations: Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics and Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

detail.title: Interpretable Health-state Estimation of Hydrogen-Fueled Solid Oxide Fuel Cells under Aviation Dynamic Environments
detail.abstract: Solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) are promising energy-conversion devices for future aviation power systems due to their high efficiency and fuel flexibility. However, health-state estimation under aviation dynamic environments remains challenging due to coupled variations in flight altitude, temperature, and pressure. To address this issue, an SOFC health-state estimation framework is proposed for aviation dynamic conditions. A one-dimensional dynamic SOFC model incorporating altitude, temperature, and pressure is first developed to represent aviation operating environments. Based on this model, multi-scale degradation mechanisms, including electrode delamination, fuel leakage, and Ni particle coarsening, are introduced to simulate degradation evolution under dynamic operating conditions. To enhance prediction accuracy and reduce input redundancy, SHAP-based feature selection is combined with a long short-term memory (LSTM) network for output-voltage prediction. Furthermore, a voltage-deviation-based health indicator (HI) is constructed to enable consistent health-state quantification across aviation and ground conditions. Results show that the proposed SHAP-LSTM model reduces RMSE and MAE by 26.2% and 33.5%, respectively, compared with a conventional LSTM. Under aviation dynamic conditions, HI degradation induced by electrode delamination and fuel leakage is 170% and 85% higher than that under ground conditions, respectively, while SHAP analysis identifies inlet temperature and pressure as key factors associated with degradation differences. The proposed framework provides an effective approach for health-state monitoring and degradation assessment of SOFC systems under dynamic aviation environments.

detail.abstract: This study examines how the absence of professionals who connect finance and information technology (IT) functions affects organizational efficiency in Pakistan. Despite the growing demand for financial and technical skills due to Pakistan's rapidly digitizing financial sector, many organizations still manage finance and IT as separate and poorly coordinated functions. Using a qualitative, case-based approach, this study examines three cases: a government institution, a private sector company (Multinet), and an analytical case study of Kohinoor Spinning Mills Limited (KOSM). Findings show that routing decisions that need both financial and technical input through separate departments causes delays ranging from several days to over a month and, in more serious cases, contributes to wider organizational and financial decline. When interview participants were introduced to the concept of integrated FinTech professionals, they independently identified this role as a way to reduce cost and delay. The study concludes that FinTech professionals are not only a technological upgrade but also a structural solution to a repeated coordination problem in Pakistani organizations. It recommends that organizations, educational institutions, and future researchers give more attention to integrating and studying this role.

title: Deciphering Asynchronous Multidimensional Microstructure Evolution for Rational Normalizing Design in Grain-oriented Electrical Steel via Machine Learning
affiliations: , Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU), Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU), Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU), Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU), Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU) and Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU)

detail.title: Deciphering Asynchronous Multidimensional Microstructure Evolution for Rational Normalizing Design in Grain-oriented Electrical Steel via Machine Learning
detail.abstract: Grain-oriented electrical steel (GOES) requires precise control of microstructural evolution to develop the concentrated Goss texture essential for high magnetic performance. Normalizing is particularly a challenging process because multiple microstructural dimensions evolve concurrently but with distinct kinetics. Quantitatively resolving this asynchronous evolution is therefore critical for rational process design, yet remains difficult with conventional descriptor-specific analyses. Here, we develop a metallurgy-informed machine learning framework that reconstructs continuous process-microstructure relationships from discrete normalizing experiments. The reconstructed process space reveals asynchronous kinetic responses across different microstructural dimensions, demonstrating distinct thermal sensitivities and coupled evolution behaviors. Metallurgical interpretation further identifies substructure-boundary coupling underlying aspect-ratio relaxation and distinct Goss-matrix boundary transitions associated with Goss evolution. These insights enable a dynamic normalizing strategy that sequentially coordinates different microstructural objectives, with its effectiveness confirmed experimentally. This work demonstrates how machine learning can translate discrete experimental observations into actionable metallurgical guidance.

title: Community and Convergence: Identity, Threat, Power, and Reciprocal Belonging

detail.title: Community and Convergence: Identity, Threat, Power, and Reciprocal Belonging

declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The work was conducted independently by the author in affiliation with The Hidden Canopy LLC.

detail.abstract: Community is often treated as context surrounding an already formed individual. This paper instead develops a mid-range theory in which community supplies the initial architecture of identity and remains part of the recursive process through which identity changes. The baseline identity structure includes membership, narrative, status maps, norms, affective associations, and expected sanctions. That structure shapes contact selection; direct and represented encounters are then filtered through institutional framing, material conditions, power, cognition, and emotion before reconstructing later identity. The paper proposes a Three-Path Model. Expansive Convergence occurs when secure identities can incorporate difference without requiring assimilation. A defensive branch distinguishes Defensive Identity, in which relative-status loss and hierarchy produce exclusionary boundary enforcement, from Protective Withdrawal, in which documented harm, coercion, discrimination, or credible vulnerability produces selective disengagement for safety. Where substantive conflict is irreconcilable, Procedural Convergence permits continued contest through legitimate rules, but only where Constitutive Convergence preserves a minimally shared political arena. The framework adds scarcity attribution, multidimensional power, elite agency, thresholds, hysteresis, de-escalation, status decoupling, and reciprocal civic belonging. It then extends the same architecture to international order, distinguishing rivalry from enmity and examining infrastructural convergence, adversarial convergence, McCarthyism, Reagan-era U.S.-China cooperation, and contemporary Sino-American de-convergence. A final political-economy layer treats capitalism, socialism, communism, authoritarianism, and utopianism as community logics rather than fixed country labels, and introduces the Socialized Floor as a hybrid mechanism through which market societies socialize selected risks, assets, or minimum-access obligations. The normative conclusion is deliberately incomplete: a durable plural community does not eliminate contradiction. It preserves equal standing and legitimate belonging across it.

title: The Forgotten Paper Record Requirement of the Help America Vote Act
affiliations: University of Michigan at Ann Arbor

detail.title: The Forgotten Paper Record Requirement of the Help America Vote Act

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that he has no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this article.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was conducted while under academic funding by Knight-Hennessy at Stanford University.

detail.abstract:
Over the past two years, federal regulation of election security has been a major focus of policymaker attention. The White House has weighed in through executive orders and by firing the leaders of the federal Election Assistance Commission; Congress, meanwhile, is considering legislation that could substantially change the law governing election administration.

It turns out that regulators have failed to enforce an important rule already enshrined in the Help America Vote Act, which provides that all voting systems used in federal elections "shall produce a permanent paper record with a manual audit capacity." Though this requirement has been in effect since 2006, it has not been routinely enforced, and many states currently fail to comply. Understanding why the gap exists-which involves an interplay between relatively weak federal bodies tasked with oversight of elections, entrenched contrary practice by state election officials, and a boom-and-bust pattern of funding for elections-provides important signals for legislators as they consider how to implement new election laws.

In addition, closing this historic enforcement gap offers a method to significantly improve election security even in the absence of new legislation. There is broad consensus among election security experts-including practitioners, academics, and intelligence agencies alike-that voterverified paper records of ballots cast are essential to protect against errors that could change election results. Despite this consensus, however, a majority of states currently allow at least some ballots to be cast over the Internet, where no such auditable paper record can be created. Moreover, in recent years, there has been a well-funded push to expand Internet voting to all voters, despite the serious risks the technology poses. Existing law is properly understood to ban this reckless approach to elections; proper enforcement would help safeguard the trustworthiness of our election system and the public's faith in our democracy.

title: Data Governance as a Foundation for Sustainable Enterprise Cloud Transformation

detail.title: Data Governance as a Foundation for Sustainable Enterprise Cloud Transformation

The author has no personal or financial relationships with any organizations that could have influenced this work.

detail.abstract: The rapid adoption of cloud computing, hybrid-cloud, and multi-cloud environments has enabled enterprises to achieve greater scalability, flexibility, resilience, and digital innovation. However, cloud migration alone does not guarantee sustainable digital transformation because organizations must address data quality, security, privacy, regulatory compliance, ownership, lifecycle management, interoperability, and responsible data use. Data governance therefore represents a foundational capability that connects cloud architecture, enterprise data management, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, compliance, sustainability, and long-term business value. Effective governance establishes the policies, accountability structures, standards, and controls required to ensure that enterprise data remains trustworthy, secure, accessible, and appropriately managed throughout the cloud transformation lifecycle (Sajja, Thipi Reddy, and Puram; Hullurappa and Addanki). Nevertheless, fragmented data environments, legacy systems, multiple cloud providers, inconsistent policies, unclear data ownership, and expanding AI workloads continue to create significant governance challenges (Sugumar; Nookala). This study critically examines how data governance enables sustainable enterprise cloud transformation and develops an integrated governance-oriented framework for secure, scalable, compliant, and environmentally responsible cloud adoption. A systematic literature review and comparative conceptual analysis were employed to synthesize contemporary perspectives on cloud governance, enterprise data management, cybersecurity, AI governance, and sustainability. The findings indicate that effective data governance improves data quality, organizational trust, security, and regulatory compliance while helping enterprises manage hybrid and multi-cloud complexity (Soundappan; Sun). The analysis further demonstrates that sustainable cloud transformation requires data lifecycle management to be embedded within architectural decisions rather than implemented after migration. Increasing AI adoption also strengthens the need for governance mechanisms that promote transparency, accountability, and responsible data management (Kommineni and Chundru). Federated and adaptive governance models provide greater flexibility for heterogeneous enterprise environments. Ultimately, sustainable cloud transformation requires balancing technological scalability with economic, environmental, security, and organizational considerations. Data governance should therefore be treated not as an administrative control added after migration, but as an architectural foundation for sustainable enterprise transformation.

title: Local Movements, Transnational Revolts: Arenas of Palestinian Solidarity
affiliations: Freie Universität, Berlin

detail.abstract: This chapter conceptualizes Palestinian solidarity protests in Germany in the context of the genocide in Gaza as multilayered arenas of contention shaped by asymmetric pressures across scales. Drawing on two and a half years of multi-sited field research it traces how activists navigated several interlinked arenas: the international arena of geopolitics that structures stakes but remains largely inaccessible; a transnational symbolic arena sustained through personal ties and platform circuits; a domestic German arena marked by memory politics, juridified boundary drawing, and securitized protest governance; and protest itself as an internal arena where solidarity is produced through co-presence and ritual. The article links these dynamics to the literature on revolutionary dynamics by treating the post-October 7 period as a quasi-revolutionary situation marked by moral shock, time compression, high contingency, and the proliferation of political agency. In this setting, coercive closure did not simply deter mobilization but, instead, redirected it toward cross-arena coordination and intensified reliance on affective infrastructures, including mediated witnessing, mutual recognition, and brokerage-an affective arrangement that stabilized grief, outrage, and moral urgency as durable commitments.

title: Complimentary-Deterrent Pricing: Reference-Price Inflation as a Congestion-Rationing Device for Shared Ancillary Services

detail.title: Complimentary-Deterrent Pricing: Reference-Price Inflation as a Congestion-Rationing Device for Shared Ancillary Services

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no financial or personal relationships that could be perceived to have influenced this work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This paper proposes future empirical studies; no data involving human participants has been collected under this submission.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding or financial support.

detail.abstract: Firms that sell access to a shared, capacity-constrained resource-a wireless network, a lounge, a support queue-face two problems at once: how to price the resource, and how to keep it from degrading once enough people use it simultaneously. This paper argues that these are not separate problems and proposes a single mechanism for both, using commercial air travel's in-flight WiFi as the illustrative case. Under complimentary-deterrent pricing (CDP), a firm (i) grants a capacity-bounded premium segment free access to the resource, funded by the premium price already paid, (ii) posts a price for the remaining, uncapped segment that is set above what a simple revenue-maximizing calculation would choose, and (iii) allows the gap between the posted price and zero to do double duty: it inflates the perceived value of the complimentary benefit for recipients (a transaction-utility effect) and it rations the shared resource by pricing out enough of the open segment to keep realized quality above a usability threshold for everyone still on it. I connect this to established work on price discrimination and versioning, reference-price and transaction-utility effects, congestion and club-good theory, and distributive versus procedural fairness, and derive from the model's own comparative statics the condition under which the mechanism stops paying for itself: as the marginal cost of resource capacity falls, the deterrence-clearing price falls with it, and the device becomes unnecessary. I offer six testable propositions, including one about a discretionary, staff-mediated variant of the mechanism that is included as exploratory rather than load-bearing, and a three-study empirical program to test the central claims.

title: Geomagnetic Ap Index (1954-2024) as a Leading Indicator of the Fed Rate (1955 -2025) (R 2 =0.9733): The Role of UV Index, Serotonin-Melatonin Balance, and Collective Optimism-Pessimism

detail.title: Geomagnetic Ap Index (1954-2024) as a Leading Indicator of the Fed Rate (1955 -2025) (R 2 =0.9733): The Role of UV Index, Serotonin-Melatonin Balance, and Collective Optimism-Pessimism

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract:
The report uses a methodological approach developed by W. S. Jevons and A. L. Chizhevsky. Solar cycle years were numbered according to the order established in solar astrophysics, grouped, and compared with the arithmetic mean values of the geomagnetic index Ap and the effective US federal funds rate with a lag of 1 year.
The results showed that the Fed's interest rate with a 1-year lag is minimal in years of extreme values (maximums and minimums) of the geomagnetic index Ap. During periods of maximum values of the geomagnetic index Ap, suppressed melatonin synthesis and the accompanying serotonin deficiency lead to increased pessimism. During periods of minimum values of the geomagnetic index Ap, which are characterized by a low ultraviolet index, insufficient serotonin synthesis and increased pessimism are observed. In both cases, collective pessimism triggers a slowdown in business activity, forcing the Federal Reserve to lower interest rates to stimulate the economy.
The coefficient of determination in the diagram average geomagnetic activity coefficient Ap - average Fed interest rate with a one-year lag is 0.9733. This means that the current year's Ap coefficient can be used to determine the forecast value of the Fed interest rate next year. The forecast value of the Fed interest rate for 2026 is 3.75%, and for 2027, 3.3%. 
The study also found a strong correlation between the geomagnetic Ap index and annual US GDP growth rates over the period 1954–2025. Annual US GDP growth rates decline significantly at extremes of the geomagnetic Ap index, prompting the Federal Reserve to lower the Fed rate with a lag of approximately one year. The projected annual US GDP growth rate for 2026 is 2.6%.

title: Leveraged and Inverse ETFs: Can Fixed-Notional Resets Stabilize Markets?
affiliations: Hanyang University

detail.title: Leveraged and Inverse ETFs: Can Fixed-Notional Resets Stabilize Markets?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has filed a patent application concerning the fixed-notional reset architecture described in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Conventional resets make leveraged and inverse exchange-traded funds buy after benchmark gains and sell after losses, so orders can cluster near the close. A fixed-notional reset transfers each day's gain or loss to or from a linked account, returning the fund to a predetermined capital base and target exposure. We ask whether this redesign can make that trading channel less procyclical or more market-stabilizing. In the model, this reverses a leveraged long fund's net benchmark trade during the reset. For an inverse fund, securities-only settlement can eliminate the order, while cash-and-securities settlement replaces it with an opposite-direction order. In a 2006–2026 historical replay, the baseline cash-and-securities version meets its trade, cash, and securities-transfer limits on 97.9% of high-volatility, large-move days; treating remaining days as conventional resets, aggregate direct orders equal 46.7% of conventional orders. Issuers and intermediaries can weigh fund-order reductions against implementation demands. Regulators can distinguish smaller fund orders from market-wide effects that depend on intermediary trading and liquidity.

title: Income Inequality Is Not Widening: Evidence from 171 Countries, 1963 to 2025

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Nothing to disclose

detail.abstract: Income inequality is not widening worldwide. We study 171 countries from 19632025, combining a longer time span and broader cross-section than the principal crosscountry studies of inequality convergence. Among 122 countries with sucient observations, 40 have signicant declining Gini trends and 25 have signicant increases; in a balanced panel, mean inequality falls from 40.34 before 2000 to 36.85 after 2015. We conrm the known convergence result in decades of additional data and show something stronger at the extremes: countries crossing a Gini of 50 subsequently fall 13.64 points on average, substantially more than matched mechanical benchmarks, and 37 of 39 nish below their own pre-peak mean. These are statements about countries rather than about people: weighting by population, the average trend is indistinguishable from zero. Broad-distribution inequality and top-income concentration move dierently, and both facts can hold at once.

title: The Invisible Working-capital Tax: Quantifying the Cost of Delayed Payments on Indian MSMEs

detail.abstract: Delayed payment is usually treated as a collection problem. This paper reframes it as a financing transfer. When a buyer pays a micro, small or medium enterprise after the contractual or statutory benchmark, the supplier is compelled to finance a portion of the buyer's operating cycle. The cost may appear as bank interest, invoice-discounting fees, foregone investment, lower cash buffers, higher default risk, or some combination of these. The paper introduces the Invisible Working-Capital Tax (IWCT) as an analytical framework for measuring the direct economic burden created by excess receivable days. The framework distinguishes excess receivables capital, marginal financing cost, collection and administration cost, expected credit-loss effects, and the opportunity cost of constrained reinvestment. It deliberately separates the direct measurable component from broader second-order effects to reduce double counting. India provides a policy-relevant setting. The Economic Survey 2025-26 estimates that approximately INR 8.1 lakh crore is locked in delayed MSME payments. A separate industry study by GAME, FISME and C2FO estimates inflationadjusted delayed receivables of INR 7.34 lakh crore as of March 2024, down from INR 10.7 lakh crore in 2022. These figures use different reference dates and methodologies and are therefore treated as distinct estimates. India also has a strong legal architecture for eligible micro and small suppliers. Section 15 of the MSMED Act requires payment within an agreed period that cannot exceed 45 days, while Section 16 provides monthly-compounded interest at three times the RBI Bank Rate for delay. The Income-tax Act reinforces this discipline by shifting the deduction for overdue payments to micro and small enterprises to an actual-payment basis. Yet complaint and resolution data indicate a substantial enforcement and bargaining-power gap. Using verified secondary sources and calibrated scenarios, the paper shows that payment delay can materially erode operating profitability even without bad debt. For an illustrative firm with INR 10 crore of annual credit sales and a 10 percent EBITDA margin, extending actual DSO from 45 to 120 days at a 12 percent marginal financing cost ties up approximately INR 2.05 crore of additional capital and creates an annual financing drag of about INR 24.66 lakh, equal to 24.7 percent of EBITDA. The paper concludes that delayed payment should be monitored as a capital-allocation and competition issue, not only as a legal dispute. It proposes an IWCT disclosure metric, automatic payment analytics, wider invoice-finance access, buyer-level payment-performance reporting, improved dispute-resolution execution, and CFOlevel receivables governance.

title: A Two-Dimensional Spectral Gap Theory for SVD Clutter Filtering in Ultrafast Plane-Wave Ultrasound Imaging
affiliations: University of Pennsylvania

detail.title: A Two-Dimensional Spectral Gap Theory for SVD Clutter Filtering in Ultrafast Plane-Wave Ultrasound Imaging

declarations.declarationOfInterest: There is no personal or financial relationship involved.
declarations.funderStatement: This is not a funded project.

detail.abstract: Alberti, Ammari, Romero, and Wintz (Mathematical Analysis of Ultrafast Ultrasound Imaging, ETH Zürich SAM Report 2016-24) gave the first rigorous derivation of the point spread function (PSF) of a plane-wave ultrasound imaging system under the Born approximation, and justified the empirical singular value decomposition (SVD) clutter filter of Demené et al. using a random model for blood-cell motion. Their statistical justification, however, is carried out only in a reduced one-dimensional model, with the explicit caveat that the two-dimensional covariance matrices are too large to analyze directly. This paper closes that gap. We extend the space-time covariance model to genuine two-dimensional particle dynamics with vector-valued drift and two-dimensional Brownian diffusion, and show that the resulting clutter covariance operator is a space-time stationary (multi-level Toeplitz-type) kernel generated by rigid translation of a compounded point spread function with a computable, essentially compact frequency support. This structure lets us invoke classical Landau-Pollak-Slepian time-and-band-limiting theory to derive an explicit, closed-form estimate for the number of significant temporal modes, and hence the appropriate SVD truncation rank K,as a function of the clutter velocity, its orientation relative to the receiver array, and the acquisition duration, independent of the number of imaged pixels. We further show that nonzero red-blood-cell diffusion destroys this coherent low-rank structure, driving the blood covariance spectrum toward a near-flat, full-rank profile that mathematically justifies treating blood as noise from the filter's perspective. We validate the resulting scaling law by direct numerical diagonalization of the derived two-dimensional covariance operators using the physical parameters of the original paper, finding the correct qualitative and approximately correct quantitative scaling with velocity, orientation, and acquisition duration. We conclude with an honest account of the theory's limitations and the open problems it leaves for a fully rigorous non-asymptotic treatment.

title: Digital Colonialism in Africa: International Law, Acquired Rights, and the Legal Continuity of Extraction

detail.title: Digital Colonialism in Africa: International Law, Acquired Rights, and the Legal Continuity of Extraction

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Nothing to declare.
declarations.funderStatement: Nothing to declare.

detail.abstract: This paper argues that digital colonialism in Africa reproduces the legal and economic structures of historical colonial extraction. Drawing on Nkrumah's theory of neocolonialism, the works of Walter Rodney, and modern African scholars, the paper demonstrates how formal political independence has not translated into economic sovereignty. Instead, extraction has simply changed form-from rubber and minerals to data. Through a case study of Facebook's Free Basics program, the paper shows how philanthropic connectivity initiatives create technical and economic dependencies that mirror colonial infrastructure development. Users are routed through corporate-controlled proxies while their data is extracted without meaningful accountability. The paper further traces the legal system enabling this extraction. The doctrine of acquired rights protected colonial-era concession agreements after independence. Contemporary bilateral investment treaties and investor-state dispute settlement mechanisms serve a similar purpose, deterring African states from enacting data localisation or privacy regulations that might conflict with foreign corporate interests. The paper concludes that digital colonialism is a combination of imperialist legal and economic structures. Understanding this continuity is the first step toward dismantling it.

title: Measuring Democratic Competence: The Democratic Competence Score (DCS) Framework

detail.title: Measuring Democratic Competence: The Democratic Competence Score (DCS) Framework

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: Claims that civic and deliberative programmes "build democratic capacity" are common, yet programme evaluation often relies on partial measures of competence and rarely separates intervention effects from background trends. This paper proposes the Democratic Competence Score (DCS), a multidimensional and counterfactual framework for measuring democratic competence at the population level. DCS decomposes competence into five complementary dimensions-civic knowledge, political efficacy, deliberative skills, critical evaluation of information, and participation in action-and combines them through geometric aggregation that penalizes imbalance across capacities. The principal analytical quantity is not a static level but change in the composite (ΔDC) and, ultimately, the counterfactual difference in that change between treatment and control territories using a differencein-differences design. A worked example demonstrates the computation from dimension scores to a programme-effect estimate. The paper positions DCS relative to established traditions in civic-competence measurement, specifies measurement and validation requirements, and treats engagement as a testable candidate mechanism of competence formation while distinguishing the participation dimension of competence from aggregate engagement metrics. An item-level measurement scale is provided in Appendix A. The contribution is a standardized, calibration-ready measurement architecture for civic education, deliberative institutions, participatory programmes, and democratic-resilience research.

detail.abstract: This dataset provides a verbatim primary source transcription of a high-stakes, late-19th-century constitutional and civic dispute in the British Straits Settlements, compiled from archival editions of the Pinang Gazette and Straits Chronicle (1887–1888) and The Daily Advertiser (1892). title: Enhancing Urban Forestry: Field Evidence and Implementation Recommendations for the Nagar Van Yojana

detail.title: Enhancing Urban Forestry: Field Evidence and Implementation Recommendations for the Nagar Van Yojana

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no personal or financial relationships with individuals or organizations that could be perceived to have influenced this study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve patients or clinical research. Primary field evidence was collected through structured visitor surveys, Key Informant Interviews, Focus Group Discussions and field observations across Nagar Van and Nagar Vatika sites.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was undertaken as part of the 2026 Embark India Development Fellowship, hosted by GRAAM with the National CAMPA, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC).

detail.abstract:
The Nagar Van Yojana (NVY) is one of the few attempts that takes urban greenery seriously as climate infrastructure, not just ornamental planting. Launched under the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016 and funded through National CAMPA, it targets 1,000 dense, climate-resilient urban forests across India by 2027. This brief is based on field work carried out during June–July 2026 across 14 Nagar Van and Nagar Vatika sites in Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan. The methods were visitor surveys, Key Informant Interviews, Focus Group Discussions and direct field observation, used to look at issues around maintenance, funding, water availability, staffing, community participation and local revenue.

The core finding is that the scheme's biggest long-term risk is not creation, but what happens after the initial funding period. More than 60% of the sites surveyed face persistent budget delays after establishment, even though the sanctioned creation budget of Rs.4 lakh per hectare is on paper adequate. Saplings are rarely the constraint. What consistently lapses is the upkeep money, and the hit falls hardest on frontline wages, dry-season irrigation and basic maintenance, particularly in the arid, alkaline Usar districts of Hardoi and Kanpur Dehat. Of all the 14 sites surveyed, only three have any working local revenue mechanism: Laharpur and Chandanpura in Bhopal and Naulakhi in Ujjain, each running a modest entry fee (Rs.12 per user). The other 11 depend entirely on state allocations. The indicative annual upkeep cost for a 50-hectare Nagar Van works out to roughly Rs.6.7 lakh (Section 6), a modest recurring burden against the one-time creation grant.

The brief proposes a blended, phased handover model. It recommends a guaranteed three-to-five-year CAMPA funding cycle for frontline wages and maintenance during the establishment phase, followed by a decentralized Public-Private-Community Partnership (PPCP) that legally enables JFMCs to monetize non-core zones through eco-tourism or regulated ticketing from year two or three onward. Scaling what has already worked in specific Nagar Vans (Etawah's off-grid solar and water management, Madhya Pradesh's cultural and community-based plantation models, Alwar's hill-top topography) would let these forests move from state dependency to community-owned civic assets.

title: From Ideas to Actions: A Public-Data Decision-Support Toolchain Across the Venture Lifecycle

detail.title: From Ideas to Actions: A Public-Data Decision-Support Toolchain Across the Venture Lifecycle

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.

declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Founders face two linked decisions across the venture lifecycle: before founding, whether an idea warrants pursuit; after founding, which operating actions and capital partners fit the company's intended trajectory. The necessary evidence is fragmented and often confined to subscription-only venture databases. We present a two-part decision-assistance toolchain built from freely available public information. Part One combines structured proposal profiling, time-bounded market and moat checks, and deterministic aggregation. Part Two reconstructs auditable investor-company event chains to analyze operating-action patterns and postinvestment behavior. We evaluate the proposal pipeline against historical outcomes and apply the toolchain in AI-inference and chip-company studies, yielding findings for both decision stages. Pre-founding. (a) After threshold selection on a 198-company development draw, the frozen system yields F 0.5 = 0.5357 [0.412, 0.655] on an independently drawn, row-disjoint 198-company validation sample; the combined 396-row benchmark estimate is 0.6301. A paired Raw LLM baseline scores 0.2734 on those 396 rows. In a separately drawn scale cohort, post-stratifying all 1,027 completed cases to the fixed execution-split composition yields 0.6506 [0.598, 0.707], with a 377-row composition-matched check yielding 0.6573. Together, these checks strengthen the evidence that performance is not confined to the original benchmark, although the incomplete scale run precludes a deployment-grade generalization claim. (b) The AI-inference market study identifies two distinct paths: distribution-layer businesses offer the most replicable route to independent profitability but face a limited revenue ceiling, whereas frontier-model ownership offers greater capital-market upside at exceptional capital cost. Post-founding. (a) Public filings, portfolio pages, company disclosures, and news can support reproducible analysis without subscription-only venture data. (b) In the chipcompany implementation, sustained product, customer, and supply-chain progress is associated with better observed outcomes; financing participation alone does not establish continuing operating progress. (c) Continued financing accounts for 79% of confirmed publicly visible post-investment actions. The evidence tentatively favors considering strategic corporate investors with relevant acquisition histories for acquisition-oriented founders, and financing-led institutional VCs with fewer observable control events for independence-oriented founders. These results offer development-stage and observational guidance, not causal guarantees or evidence of large-scale deployment performance; they neither rank investors nor constitute investment advice. Beyond the empirical findings, we release an end-to-end reproducibility stack-shared ontology, provenance-bearing EventChain data, schemas, benchmarks, and executable skills-so the complete workflow can be audited, reused, and extended.

detail.abstract: Historical financial research can fail before a return series is joined. A database may attach a fact to its fiscal period end, retain only the latest comparative value, or continue serving a number after an issuer has withdrawn reliance on the underlying financial statements. Each design can place information into a historical decision that was not admissible at that time. This paper presents the AhaSignals Financial AI Point-in-Time Integrity Benchmark v1.1, an openbook, deterministic conformance suite built from accession-level U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission filings. The benchmark contains eight purposively selected cases, five issuers, four failure families and sixteen prompts across evidence-restricted retrieval and knowledgecontamination tracks. It uses SEC acceptance timestamps as an auditable regulatory event clock and requires the tested system to cite the controlling accession, exclude later filings, preserve evidence-state changes and abstain during a non-reliance interval. A deliberately contaminated calibration response is rejected as a temporal-integrity failure. In one AhaSignals-operated pilot, a financial AI system returned sixteen conforming responses, with no temporal-integrity failures; this is an execution-chain result, not a general model ranking. In the studied CoreWeave source set, a latest-value query replaces all fourteen matched facts in an earlier decision set and reverses the sign of one reported value. A BigBear.ai ledger preserves 160 non-zero issuerlabelled corrections across the previously reported, non-reliance and restated states. These are deterministic case results, not market-frequency estimates. The contribution is a small, fully auditable test of whether a financial system obeys the information clock before it computes a factor or backtest.

detail.abstract: Digital tools have become the core infrastructure of modern civilisation, yet large segments of the global population remain inactive despite full access. This essay introduces a dual-entropy frameworkpersonal entropy and institutional entropy-to explain why individuals and societies fail to activate available knowledge. Using decision-science and game-theoretic modelling, the essay demonstrates how digital inactivation reduces productivity, weakens trust, and slows knowledge accumulation. It argues that activation, not access, is the central economic variable of the 21st century. Without reducing entropy, humanity cannot accelerate knowledge fast enough to reach advanced frontiers such as artificial stellar engineering. The essay concludes that autonomous digital systems and long-horizon planetary institutions will become the primary trust infrastructure, enabling multigenerational projects that extend into the million-and billion-year frontier.

title: Technology Governance in the Age of AI: From Redistribution to Predistribution

detail.title: Technology Governance in the Age of AI: From Redistribution to Predistribution

detail.abstract: What should we do about labor automation in the age of artificial intelligence? Early proposals such as Universal Basic Income focused on taxing and redistributing the proceeds of AI. Now, an emerging slate of ideas tagged to the concept of "predistribution" proposes distributing ownership through citizen stakes in AI or sovereign wealth funds. But what is "predistribution"? This Article presents a positive and unifying theory of predistribution, describes its categories, and explains how it can remake work in the age of AI. For over a century, Americans have focused on tax-and-transfer redistribution to address income inequality in the realm of consumption while calibrating tax policy to produce the right mix of forward incentives for production. Predistribution encompasses the ways of intervening in the realm of production before market outcomes are produced for consumption. This Article defines "predistribution" as the distribution of power over economic outcomes and identifies four categories of predistribution: (1) incentives and bargaining power, (2) public production, (3) ownership, and (4) governance and control.

title: Input Supply and the Design of AI Research Subsidies

detail.abstract: We study which inputs a temporary AI research subsidy should reimburse. In a benchmark with homogeneous research, one knowledge externality, separable input-supply costs and no existing subsidies, marginal welfare per fiscal dollar is higher for the more elastically supplied input. We embed this principle in dynamic general equilibrium with education, compute investment and electricity constraints. An anchored occupational frontier preserves all balanced-growth stocks, allocations, prices and expenditures while computed policy rankings reverse. Joint calibration combines expenditure, compensation and input-cost observations with occupational-supply proxies. For an eight-year program, common-rate wage-and-compute support yields consumption-equivalent welfare gains 0.94 percent above compute-only when researcher supply matches a long-run computer-scientist response. Matching the same source's first-year response instead, with the resulting curve held fixed across dates, puts joint support 29.76 percent below compute-only at the identical balanced-growth allocation. An alternative input-composition map also reverses the ranking at the same assumed knowledge spillover. Absolute welfare gains are small at the evaluated budget. These comparisons show why supply measurement over the relevant policy horizon is central to subsidy design, beyond matching equilibrium expenditures.

title: Sign preservation in linear rational expectations models

detail.title: Sign preservation in linear rational expectations models

detail.abstract: This paper introduces sign preservation as a robustness criterion for selecting among fundamental equilibria in linear rational expectations models. An equilibrium is sign-preserving if the orientation of its general-equilibrium multiplier with respect to the exogenous shocks is maintained as their persistence varies over its admissible range, ruling out system-wide sign reversals associated with singularities of the equilibrium mapping. The analysis relates sign preservation to established equilibrium-selection criteria, including determinacy, forward convergence and the minimum-modulus solution. While other criteria depend on the modulus of the unselected roots of the system, sign preservation is determined only by the real positive ones. Still, a general result can be stated: when forward convergence holds throughout the admissible range of shock persistence, which is guaranteed under determinacy, the minimum-modulus solution is always sign-preserving. Under appropriate restrictions, implications can be drawn from sign preservation to forward convergence and determinacy. The framework, applied to the canonical New Keynesian model, shows that neo-Fisherian responses arise when the policy-shock persistence crosses the forward-convergence threshold, coinciding with a system-wide reversal in the equilibrium multiplier rather than reflecting a distinct interest-rate--inflation mechanism.

detail.abstract: We design a novel survey to study how education shapes households’ joint beliefs about inflation, unemployment, and monetary policy transmission. College-educated respondents perceive the inflation-unemployment trade-off and hold views similar to professional forecasters, while less educated respondents favor supply-side narratives. When exposed to hypothetical monetary policy interventions, the more educated update expectations and adjust consumption and saving in line with standard models, whereas the less educated display greater rigidity. This education gradient persists after controlling for information sources, financial literacy, and institutional trust, pointing to differences in abstract reasoning. Open-ended responses are consistent with college-educated households holding mental models aligned with standard macroeconomic theory.

detail.abstract: Characteristic-based factor models can fit returns identically while attributing them differently to latent, observed-factor, and intercept components. We show how an inner product on characteristic space selects this decomposition and formulate its loading class modulo latent rotations. For an exactly profiled estimator with deterministic date weights and an estimated Gram metric, we derive a linear representation retaining both return-score and metric uncertainty. Smooth reports admit chart-invariant inference and feasible long-run covariance estimation. Covariance alignment provides sufficient conditions for structural interpretation with a fixed cross section. Near a smooth exposure boundary, metric estimation also moves the feasible set. Joint Gaussian projection yields drift-robust scalar confidence intervals. For one constraint, the least-favorable tail envelopes reduce to the interior and binding endpoints. Numerical experiments distinguish omitted metric uncertainty from omitted boundary movement.

title: When Virtual Reality Is Worth the Investment: A Two-Layer Systematic Review of Global Research, Economic Evidence, and Cost-Value Decision Making

detail.title: When Virtual Reality Is Worth the Investment: A Two-Layer Systematic Review of Global Research, Economic Evidence, and Cost-Value Decision Making

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declare no conflicts of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: A country can publish thousands of virtual reality (VR) papers and still leave a hospital, factory, or ministry without a defensible investment case. This review separates three quantities that the literature routinely conflates: research intensity, domain specialization, and economic evidence. Layer 1 is a reproducible OpenAlex bibliometric census of English-language journal articles and reviews whose title or abstract contains "virtual reality," indexed as of 6-7 September 2026, with a publication-year window of 2006-2026 (incomplete coverage of 2026): N_global = 85,535 unique works. Authorship attributions rank the United States (15,078), China (11,898), the United Kingdom (5,665), Germany (3,951), Italy (3,390), South Korea (3,085), and Canada (3,060) as the largest producers. Domain filters show U.S. and U.K. concentration in healthcare and surgical training, Chinese concentration in engineering, construction, and industrial VR, and a thin corporate-training literature in every country. A title-abstract economic-phrase subset contains 1,255 works; that count is a filter total, not an inclusion set. Layer 2 is a single-reviewer, PRISMA 2020-informed economic systematic review with search cutoff 7 September 2026: 1,158 unique records screened, 155 sought and retrieved for full-record assessment, 106 excluded at full record, and N_economic = 49 included (28 direct monetary or formal economic analyses; 10 indirect implementation papers; 11 reviews). VR is rarely shown to reduce first-use total cost. It more often reduces a named cost object-instructor or live-drill staff time, wet-lab consumables, travel, or operating-room teaching minutes-or purchases a better outcome at higher capital cost, or becomes cheaper only after reuse. No eligible primary economic evaluation was identified for China, Japan, South Korea, France, or Italy in the English-language sources and country-directed searches conducted for this review through 7 September 2026, despite high Layer-1 output. This does not establish that no such study exists in other languages, subscription databases, or sources not searched. The VR Cost-Value Decision Framework (VR-CVDF) requires institutions to name the comparator, the cost object, C₀, Cᵣ, N, ΔE, and evidence strength before claiming that VR is worth the investment.

title:
The UK Productivity Puzzle 
Causes, Empirical Analysis, and Policy Implications

detail.title:
The UK Productivity Puzzle 
Causes, Empirical Analysis, and Policy Implications

detail.abstract:
The UK Productivity Puzzle refers to the persistent stagnation of productivity growth in the United Kingdom following the 2008 Global Financial Crisis, despite relatively strong employment performance. This paper investigates the underlying causes of this divergence using both qualitative analysis and empirical regression modelling. It argues that the slowdown in labour productivity is the result of a combination of cyclical demand-side weaknesses and deeper structural inefficiencies within the economy. 

Key contributing factors include prolonged weakness in aggregate demand, underinvestment in physical and human capital, slow diffusion of innovation, labour market adjustments, and inefficient allocation of resources, including the persistence of zombie firms. A time series regression model is estimated over the period 1971 to 2025 to quantify the relationship between labour productivity and its principal determinants. A qualitative comparative analysis with the United States highlights how differences in policy responses and economic adjustment mechanisms influenced recovery trajectories. The findings suggest that resolving the productivity puzzle requires long-term structural reforms rather than short-term cyclical measures.

title: The Architecture of Market Regimes: Modeling DXY through Structural and Reflexive Layers Expanded and Consolidated Edition

detail.title: The Architecture of Market Regimes: Modeling DXY through Structural and Reflexive Layers Expanded and Consolidated Edition

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Hello
declarations.funderStatement: Hello

detail.abstract: Traditional models attempting to explain the dynamics of the U.S. Dollar Index (DXY)— such as Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) or simple interest-rate differential frameworks— consistently fail to capture real-world fluctuations, particularly during episodes of financial stress. These models are largely linear, neglecting the financial microstructure (“plumbing”) and assuming static correlations. This work constructs a state-dependent, non-linear in tegrated equation to describe the DXY’s value. We hypothesize that DXY is a complex function of the ratio between Global Effective Demand (D∗) and Global Effective Supply (S∗) for the USD. The core innovation lies in introducing a systemic “stress” variable (σsys), which renders the model’s weights (α,β) and convexity (κsys) as dynamic functions rather than constants. Furthermore, we introduce foundational meta-variables—Geopolitical Power (Gpol), Internal U.S. Risk (RUS), and Human Capital (Hcap)—not as direct inputs but as modulators altering the system’s internal behavior. This model provides a stronger frame work for capturing non-linear properties, especially the convex “flight-to-quality” response of the USD. This edition expands that argument into a full specification, tests it, and applies it. Part I builds the model in six strata. Layer 0 is the mechanical ratio of ten demand channels to seven supply channels. Layer 1 replaces the original’s raw stress thermometer with a bounded systemic instability index σsys ∈ [0,1], so that the safe-haven term is convex without being explosive. Layer 2 supplies the structural and trust variables—shelter credibility Φsys and the share sUS,sys of global flight-to-quality flow that the dollar actually captures—as functions of geopolitical power, internal U.S. risk, institutional trust Mtrust and geopolitical fragmentation Tfrag. Layer 3 makes the convexity exponent κsys an explicit function of leverage, crisis memory Mshock and reflexivity. Layer 4 adds two psycho-technical states, the homogeneity of collective belief Hsoc and impulse efficiency Iimp, which amplify Layer 3 and are shown to form a simultaneous system with a unique fixed point under a stated and checkable condition. Layer 5 introduces a secular structural-integrity coefficient Ψstr(t), equal to one when the dollar’s position is intact and falling along a cliff rather than a slope as alternative infrastructure and fragmentation accumulate. Every elasticity in the model interpolates between a calm value and a crisis value through a shared logistic transition in σsys; the specification is assembled, its comparative statics derived, and its identification stated. Part II confronts the model with eleven episodes—the 2008 financial crisis, COVID-19, the taper episodes, U.S. debt-ceiling standoffs, the trade war, the 2022 sanctions on Russia, stablecoin growth, carrier-power and digital-substrate scenarios, and the 2025 tariff episode— reading each one term by term through the log-linear form and scoring predictions against iv v observation in a single cross-case table. Hypothetical cases are kept as hypotheticals and paired with real analogues where any exist. Part III turns the model on policy: the anatomy of an inflation crisis in a psycho reflexive era, a lever-by-lever playbook with legal basis and dated historical activations, the execution rhythm and the structural traps it must avoid, the coordination mechanism among the major central banks, and the 1971 inflection that created the system being modelled. Throughout, three commitments hold. No number enters the text without a source. No reference enters the bibliography without verification.

title: Put your money where your mouth is? Experimental evidence of an intention-behavior gap in the support for solar and wind energy
affiliations: Brandenburg University of Technology Cottbus-Senftenberg, Brandenburg University of Technology (BTU), Brandenburg University of Technology Cottbus-Senftenberg and Brandenburg University of Technology Cottbus-Senftenberg

detail.title: Put your money where your mouth is? Experimental evidence of an intention-behavior gap in the support for solar and wind energy
detail.abstract: We quantify differences between the stated and revealed support for wind and solar energy in a controlled and pre-registered lab experiment. We implemented a 2 x 2 between-subject design and varied the energy type (wind or solar) as well as preference type (stated or revealed). We find strong evidence for an intention-behavior gap in the support for both energy types: The stated support was significantly higher than the revealed support for wind and solar energy, even after controlling for potential confounding factors. Our results provide evidence that a lower-than-expected level of revealed support for renewable energy projects can be explained in part by skepticism, which remains undetected in stated preferences methods.

title: A Pre-registered, Cryptographically Timestamped Proving Protocol for Directional Market Forecasting, with Announced Echo State Network and Quantum Reservoir Computing Examinations

detail.title: A Pre-registered, Cryptographically Timestamped Proving Protocol for Directional Market Forecasting, with Announced Echo State Network and Quantum Reservoir Computing Examinations

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests. The author is the sole developer of the Quandiction project described in the paper; no external party has influenced the design or reporting of the study.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. All work was self-funded by the author.

detail.abstract: Directional forecasting claims about markets are, in common practice, unfalsifiable: the search behind a published strategy is unreported, the benchmark is chosen alongside the results, and failed attempts leave no record. We present a proving protocol that makes such claims checkable without trusting the authors. Every evaluative decision is committed to a cryptographically timestamped append-only record before it can be compared with outcomes. We report the protocol's first completed application: a baseline stage across five market target streams, in which four model paradigms — from regularized linear models to a large language model — all failed to exceed floors set by a pre-registered naive family operating on price alone, net of costs. The floors, the statistical machinery (a cumulative hypothesis family under Romano-Wolf stepdown control, validated on synthetic ground truth), and the enforcement patterns that make protocol violations machine-detectable or impossible by construction are published in full. On this record we announce, in registered-report form, the project's next examinations: an echo state network stage, and a quantum reservoir stage evaluated as the symmetric difference ∆ against an exactly twinned classical arm. To our knowledge this is the first pre-registered forward test of quantum reservoir computing against a matched classical counterpart in financial forecasting. The design invariants are timestamped with this paper; the full designs undergo registered-report review before any run. Their outcomes, and the per-arm grid of the baseline stage, are published in a separate results report under the disclosure policy fixed here, whatever the sign of ∆.

title: Reframing "Habits" As Distinct "Economic Goods": A Novel "Individual Habit-Based Consumer Theory"

detail.title: Reframing "Habits" As Distinct "Economic Goods": A Novel "Individual Habit-Based Consumer Theory"

detail.abstract: Purpose: This paper establishes a novel theoretical framework (Individual Habit-Based Consumer Theory) to reframe automatic habits as distinct economic goods, formalizing habit loop mechanics within rational choice theory to explain persistent, seemingly irrational human behaviors. Design/methodology/approach: The study develops an axiomatic microeconomic optimization model. Habits are treated as endogenous goods with non-monetary prices derived from automaticity, inconsistency, and cue frequency, optimized under a constrained behavioral resource budget. Findings: Cumulative repetition endogenously lowers a habit’s behavioral price, creating a lock-in effect. This frames the intention-behavior gap as an economic optimization under high initial switching costs rather than psychological failure. Research limitations/implications: As a pure theoretical framework, this research lacks empirical validation. Future paradigms must experimentally test the proposed hypotheses using neuroimaging or automated behavioral tracking data collected via wearable technologies. Practical implications: Motivational interventions are inefficient if a behavior's initial resource barrier is too high. Practitioners should prioritize environmental choice architecture that systematically lowers the dynamic price of desirable habits through task simplification. Social implications: Policymakers can leverage this framework to scale public health and environmental campaigns. Shifting from information dissemination to structural cue design optimizes population welfare under limited cognitive or temporal resource constraints. Originality/value: This paper is the first to mathematically formalize the psychological habit loop within individual consumer theory. It uniquely redefines behavioral inertia as a structural problem of resource allocation under dynamic pricing.

title: When Prejudice Hits Home: Hate Crime and the Market for Mortgage Credit
affiliations: University of St Andrews Business School, Fordham University  , University of Glasgow and Durham University Business School

detail.title: When Prejudice Hits Home: Hate Crime and the Market for Mortgage Credit
detail.abstract: Using data covering the near-universe of U.S. mortgage applications, we show that racial hate crimes are linked to significantly lower local mortgage demand. The decline is specific to racial hate crimes, and no comparable pattern arises for general crime or non-hate offenses. Decomposing exposure into incidents against a borrower’s own group and against other groups, we find that both minority and White applicants apply less, minority applicants mainly after incidents against their own group (targeted threat) and White applicants after incidents against other groups (generalized fear). We also employ a difference-in-differences design around the 2020 surge in hate crime, and the results point in the same direction. Counties with more racial hate crimes show higher psychological distress, lower visible consumption, and weaker home sales and house-price growth, while rents show no comparable change, consistent with effects concentrated in owner-occupied housing.

title: Ranking, Not Estimating: Out-Of-Sample Validation of Machine Learning on the UN Food Loss and Waste Database
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Ranking, Not Estimating: Out-Of-Sample Validation of Machine Learning on the UN Food Loss and Waste Database
