detail.abstract: This article examines the exercise of stop and search powers by the Nigeria Police Force and the extent to which the legal protections available to citizens against arbitrary intrusion are realised in practice. It examines policing power whose roots in Nigeria lie in the colonial era, and situates stop and search in light of the Nigerian legal framework, comprising constitutional guarantees, the Nigeria Police Act 2020, and international human rights instruments, against the comparative approaches of England and Wales, the United States, and South Africa. It also examines the specific rights available to a citizen who is stopped or searched and the remedies open to one whose rights are violated, set against the documented reality of abuse, extortion, and impunity in police-citizen encounters. For the purpose of this study, this work adopts the doctrinal method, relying on constitutional and statutory provisions, judicial authorities, and international instruments, supplemented by the empirical findings of human rights organisations and previous researchers on policing in Nigeria. This article, at the end of its findings, identifies that Nigeria's legal framework contains substantive protections capable of shielding citizens from arbitrary stop and search. However, this work finds that the colonial heritage of Nigerian policing, chronic underfunding, lack of effective accountability mechanisms, and a culture of impunity conspire to render these protections largely illusory in practice. This work therefore, based on these findings, proposes the reforms necessary to bridge the gap between law and practice.

title: Regulating Political Power, Political Parties under Nepalese Electoral Law

detail.title: Regulating Political Power, Political Parties under Nepalese Electoral Law

declarations.declarationOfInterest: n/a
declarations.funderStatement: n/a

detail.abstract:
Political parties occupy a constitutionally significant position in Nepal’s democratic order, functioning simultaneously as voluntary associations and principal institutions through which political power is organized and exercised. This paper examines the extent to which Nepalese electoral law regulates political parties while preserving political freedom, associational autonomy, democratic pluralism, and electoral integrity. It analyses the constitutional and statutory framework governing political party formation and registration, internal democracy, inclusive representation, legislative discipline, party mergers and splits, political finance, and dispute resolution, with particular attention to the Constitution of Nepal, 2015, the Political Parties Act, 2073 (2017), the Political Parties Regulation, 2074 (2017), and the Election Commission Act, 2073 (2017). The study adopts a doctrinal legal research methodology, examining legislation, administrative instruments, Election Commission practices, and relevant decisions of the Supreme Court of Nepal.

The paper argues that Nepal has developed a comparatively comprehensive formal framework for regulating political parties, but that a substantial disjuncture persists between legal prescription and institutional enforcement. Constitutional requirements concerning periodic internal elections, inclusive representation, and financial disclosure provide important safeguards against oligarchic party structures and opaque political financing. Nevertheless, weak investigative capacity, limited scrutiny of financial disclosures, inadequate verification of internal democratic practices, and an ineffective hierarchy of sanctions constrain the practical effectiveness of these safeguards. The analysis further identifies tensions within anti-defection and party-split regulations, particularly where statutory mechanisms become instruments of short-term political strategy. The paper therefore contends that effective regulation should not diminish legitimate party autonomy but should strengthen accountable self-government through enhanced Election Commission oversight, independent political-finance auditing, calibrated sanctions, transparent candidate-selection procedures, and greater financial transparency. Such reforms are essential to transform Nepal’s existing formal regime of regulated pluralism into a more substantively democratic system of political accountability.

title: Shadows of Consciousness: An Investigation into Ionic Neural Networks Using the Neurotransmitter Ion Receptor Glial Endocannabinoid Network (NIRGEN) Paradigm

detail.title: Shadows of Consciousness: An Investigation into Ionic Neural Networks Using the Neurotransmitter Ion Receptor Glial Endocannabinoid Network (NIRGEN) Paradigm

declarations.declarationOfInterest: na
declarations.ethicsApproval: na
declarations.funderStatement: Self Funded

detail.abstract:
Picture trying to understand a symphony orchestra from the lobby, with one low-quality microphone taped to the back wall. You can hear that something is happening, \textit{scilicet} volume rising and falling, crescendos, silence between movements, but yet not the oboe, not the second violins entering a half-beat late, and certainly not that eighty different instruments are involved, each capable of a sound no other can make. A theory built only from that microphone would be a theory of loudness over time and nothing else.

This is almost exactly what happened. In 1943 the only signal recoverable from outside a neuron was a voltage trace. McCulloch and Pitts built a model from it. Nine years later Hodgkin and Huxley proved that voltage is the microphone reading.  That is, they showed that voltage is the derived epiphenomenon of discrete ions moving through specific molecular gates in integer steps, subject to conservation laws and finite molecular inventories. The artificial lineage kept the voltage and went backstage without us.

This paper goes backstage to explore the biological mechanisms that were discoverd after the 1943 formalism. More specifically, I review through 6 biological threads of literature which document what was there: ions that are chemically non-interchangeable; receptors that count a fixed integer number of ligands before a fixed ionic quantum translocates; a glial layer that continuously renegotiates the capacity ceiling within which synaptic computation occurs; retrograde endocannabinoid signaling by which the postsynaptic neuron instructs its own upstream neighbor locally and without any global error signal, a discovery delayed thirty years in part by cannabis prohibition under the Marihuana Tax Act of 1937. An audit of twenty-three model classes from McCulloch--Pitts through GPT-3 against five of these finds that none represent all five, and most represent none. From this I derive the Neurotransmitter Ion Receptor Glial Endocannabinoid Network (NIRGEN) Framework.  

From this basic framework many different model classes arise naturally as a result of the prevailing literature that I review in this research.  I design and study the first class of NIRGEN models herein: a discrete, biophysically grounded Ionic Neural Network (INN) in which computation proceeds through conservation laws of ions of a single species, geometric ion capacity limits, and stoichiometric thresholds. A single unit solves XOR by saturation rather than geometric transformation.  I conclude the result with the design of three experiments to ground the formalism empirically and to demonstrate how one can use the corresponding \href{https://github.com/drmylesgarveylabs/nirgen}{nirgen Github Package} to begin to explore their own "INN" model designs. This paper in effect studies the orchestra juxtaposed against the  microphone in the lobby for which was the primary unit of study for more than 80 years.

detail.abstract: A number of new European Union (EU) law acts dealing with the digital economy reference fairness as one of their main goals or benchmarks, which has sparked renewed interest in the normative meaning of fairness and the role it plays in the regulation of the digital market. This paper draws on a private law theory of justice, that of commutative justice, to propose a reading of the term fairness within these acts and their new legal instruments, which is grounded in the principles of private law exchanges. Because access to and fair exchanges on digital markets lie at the heart of these acts, we develop a normative reconstruction of specific provisions of the acts that is based on an analysis of commutative justice and that provides a conceptual framework for interpreting and sharpening their objectives and instruments. In doing so, this paper wants to shed light on this central aspect of fairness and its implications for the emerging EU framework governing digital markets.

detail.abstract: Complex enterprises must integrate data across legacy applications, software-as-a-service platforms, operational databases, partner networks, cloud services, analytical platforms, and emerging artificial-intelligence workloads. Cloud architecture expands the available integration mechanisms, yet greater connectivity can also multiply copies, dependencies, semantic conflicts, security boundaries, and operational failure modes. This structured technical review synthesizes research and authoritative guidance on cloud computing, distributed data systems, warehouses and lakes, lakehouse architecture, event streaming, data mesh, governance, zero trust, reliability, and continuity. It asks how enterprises should combine integration styles, shared platforms, and distributed ownership without imposing either brittle centralization or uncontrolled fragmentation. The evidence indicates that no single mechanism-batch pipelines, application programming interfaces (APIs), events, replication, federation, or common storage-is sufficient for every workload. Effective architectures select patterns according to latency, consistency, autonomy, volume, and regulatory requirements; establish contracts and shared semantics; embed identity, lineage, quality, and policy controls; and operate integration as a measurable product capability. The paper proposes CONNECT: Context and capability requirements, Ownership and operating model, Networked integration patterns, Normalized semantics and contracts, Embedded security and governance, Continuous observability and reliability, and Transition, portability, and lifecycle. CONNECT is an evidence-derived conceptual framework, not an empirically validated model. Its contribution is to connect technical integration choices with governance, accountability, and evolutionary change in hybrid and multi-cloud enterprise ecosystems.

detail.abstract: Norges Bank Investment Management's September 2026 proposal to cut government bonds from 70% to 50% of its benchmark triggered widespread concern about a Treasury "exodus." This paper argues that framing is misplaced: the reallocation is a gradual, ministry-pending shift within dollar assets, not an exit from them, and is trivial relative to average daily Treasury turnover. However, dismissing the episode entirely misses a more consequential fault line. Drawing on Federal Reserve research showing that Treasury market depth thins precisely as volatility rises, the paper distinguishes between a reallocation's size and its capacity to trigger disorderly selling if it coincides with other stress signals — weak auctions, widening spreads, dollar strength, and leveraged deleveraging. The analysis then traces the transmission channel to India: while the Reserve Bank of India's reserve diversification is structurally different from NBIM's (precautionary and central-bank-driven rather than yield-seeking), India remains exposed to the global financial cycle through which US term-premium shocks transmit to emerging-market yields, currencies, and risk premia. Applying the Rey/Miranda-Agrippino global financial cycle framework alongside IMF and World Bank research on nonbank intermediation and US rate shocks, the paper constructs three scenario-based, judgment-weighted forecasts (base, adverse, benign) for US and Indian 10-year yields, USD/INR, and gold through early 2028, with corresponding portfolio-positioning implications. The central claim is that Norway's letter is a symptom of rising US term premia rather than an independent cause of EM stress, and that India's genuine vulnerability lies in a fiscal-inflation shock materializing alongside — not within — such reallocations

detail.abstract: This article examines the mandatory pre-trial claims procedure governing disputes with railway carriers under Russian law. It considers the required content of a claim, the documentary record that must accompany it, permissible methods of service, the persons entitled to assert transport claims, and the legal consequences of missing the six-month and forty-five-day claim periods. The article argues that those periods are not peremptory and do not extinguish the claimant's substantive right where the statutory claims procedure is ultimately completed and the action is filed within the applicable limitation period. detail.abstract: Deposits are gathered in local markets and priced nationally. We measure the pricing directly from the assignment of branches to rate-setting accounts: in June 2022, 94 percent of banks with five or more linked branches posted one certificate rate network-wide, and the share held through the 2023 failures. Outflows nonetheless had a geography inside the bank that the stress did not create: a bank's branches in denser markets and where its franchise is large lose ground nearly every year since 2015. In 2023, mean branch growth fell from nine percentage points to below zero, and gradients of 0.7 and 2.1 per standard deviation allocated losses rather than growth. Posted rates moved with these characteristics by about a basis point, against 492 basis points of tightening, and banks quoting several rates internally were no exception. Depositor traits thought to make funding loyal leave no trace in the price either.

detail.abstract: We examine how sustainability uncertainty influences firms' adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) by assessing whether companies expand their AI-skilled workforce when facing ambiguity in environmental, social, and governance (ESG) conditions. Using the ESG-based Sustainability Uncertainty Index (ESGUI) (Ongan et al., 2025) and the resume-based AI workforce measure (Babina et al., 2024), we provide firm-level evidence on this relationship. Employing fixed effects, matching techniques, and instrumental-variable strategies exploiting exogenous variation in sustainability uncertainty, we find that higher uncertainty leads to a larger AI workforce, consistent with an adaptation hypothesis in which firms strengthen analytical capabilities under ambiguity. The effect is weaker among highly leveraged firms and stronger among firms with greater cash reserves and R&D intensity, indicating that financial flexibility and innovation capacity shape responses to ESG-related uncertainty.

detail.abstract: Enterprise data migration to cloud environments changes where information is stored, processed, administered, monitored, and legally exposed. Although cloud services offer elasticity, automation, and managed security capabilities, migration can amplify risk when organizations transfer data without resolving classification, ownership, identity, encryption, residency, lineage, retention, and recovery requirements. This structured technical review synthesizes scholarly research and authoritative guidance on cloud computing, data governance, zero trust, information-security controls, distributed data systems, privacy, operational resilience, and cloud data architecture. The evidence shows that migration risk is concentrated in transitions: incomplete inventories, uncontrolled copies, overprivileged migration tools, insecure temporary storage, inconsistent policy translation, data-integrity failures, and premature decommissioning. Provider controls do not transfer accountability from the enterprise, and compliance attestations do not by themselves establish workload-specific assurance. The paper proposes the MIGRATE framework: Map data and obligations; Identify ownership and decision rights; Govern destination and provider controls; Restrict identities and migration paths; Assure integrity, lineage, and recoverability; Transition through controlled waves; and Evidence, evaluate, and exit. MIGRATE integrates technical safeguards with governance gates before, during, and after transfer. It is a conceptual synthesis and has not been empirically validated. Its main implication is that secure cloud migration should be governed as a reversible lifecycle of data-state transitions rather than as a one-time infrastructure relocation.

detail.abstract: This research paper aimed to investigate a novel intersection in human resource management within modern healthcare, how artificial intelligence (AI)-driven administrative tools influence retention intentions among physicians  and nurses amid hybrid (in-person and telemedicine) work models. Drawing on the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) theory, the study proposed that techno-stress and POS mediate the relationship between AI automation intensity and retention intentions. Data from a cross-sectional survey of 310 physicians and nurses across 15 hospitals in urban and semi-rural settings were collected between 2025-2026 and were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) with bootstrapping for mediation tests. Study found significant mediation by techno-stress and POS between AI automation and retention intention. This study added POS as a mediator in the sequential mediation model; novel result appeared for POS as it was used as a moderator previously. Implications for HR policy, including targeted AI literacy training and support mechanisms, are discussed. This study contributes to emerging literature on technology-induced HR challenges in healthcare.
